entries.title: Watery lentil soup, attempt one
entries.body: Okay, so last night I meal-prepped for the first time in maybe a year. Lentil soup, because the internet said it was impossible to mess up. The internet was wrong. I used too much broth and it came out closer to lentil tea. I still portioned it into four containers and brought one to work today. Ate it at my desk at 12:40 while answering Slack, which is not the lunch break I keep telling myself I deserve. Marcus walked by and asked if I was drinking soup out of a mug on purpose. I was not. Total cost for the whole batch was about nine dollars, so even watery it beats the twelve dollar salad place downstairs. Next time, less broth and maybe some actual spices. Frankly, I'm counting this as a win just because I didn't order takeout tonight.
entries.highlight: Tried meal prepping lentil soup for the first time in a year; it came out watery but saved money on lunches.

entries.title: Dumplings with Sam until closing
entries.body: Met Sam at the dumpling place near my apartment after work. I almost canceled because I was tired, and I'm really glad I didn't. We got the pork and chive ones and the cucumber salad, and then ordered a second round of dumplings because we were talking too much to notice we were still hungry. Sam told the story about our sophomore year fire alarm again, the one where I came out holding a frying pan for no reason, and I laughed so hard the people at the next table looked over. We stayed until they started stacking chairs at 10. My half was $31, which I will be pretending is not part of the eating out problem. Sam asked how work was and I said fine, which is what I say when it is not really fine. Something to think about.
entries.highlight: Had a long dinner with college friend Sam and laughed about old stories, though work stress came up.

entries.title: The takeout number was $412
entries.body: Did a budget check-in tonight, which for me means opening my banking app and wincing. I finally added up everything I spent on takeout and eating out this month and it came to $412. In November. And the month isn't even over. Most of it is the Thai place and the dumpling place, plus a bunch of eleven dollar lunches I don't even remember eating. Rent is $1,650 and I keep saying I want to move somewhere with more light, but at this rate I'll be saving for that until I'm sixty. I made a very basic spreadsheet with four columns: rent, bills, groceries, everything else. It's ugly but it exists. The plan is to check it every Friday. We'll see if Friday me is as motivated as Friday night me feels right now.
entries.highlight: Added up the month's takeout spending, was shocked at $412, and started a simple budget spreadsheet.

entries.title: Mom is putting the garden to bed
entries.body: Called Mom on the walk home from the train. It was already dark at 5:15, which I will never get used to. She spent the weekend putting the garden to bed for the winter, pulling the last tomato plants and planting garlic for next summer. She says garlic is the only crop that rewards patience, and then said that's why she likes it, which felt pointed. Dad got on for a minute to say hi. His knee is acting up with the cold and he's been grumbling about the stairs to the basement. We talked about Thanksgiving logistics: I'm on stuffing and pie, same as every year. I said I'd try a homemade crust and Mom made a noise like she didn't believe me. We talked for over an hour and I walked two extra blocks just to keep going.
entries.highlight: Had an hour-long call with Mom about her winter garden, Dad's sore knee, and Thanksgiving plans.

entries.title: Thanksgiving eve pie at my parents'
entries.body: Took a half day and caught the 2:40 train to my parents'. Mom had the kitchen ready for me the second I walked in, like a surgeon prepping an operating room. I made the stuffing base tonight so it can just go in the oven tomorrow, and then the pie. I said I'd do a homemade crust, and I did try, but it cracked into about nine pieces, so I quietly used the store-bought backup I'd hidden in my bag. Mom saw the box and said nothing, which is worse than saying something. Dad tasted the filling off the spoon and said it was the best one yet. He says that every year. The house smells like cinnamon and onions and I'm on the couch with tea. Tomorrow is the actual dinner, but to be fair, tonight is my favorite part.
entries.highlight: Took the train to their parents' and made the Thanksgiving stuffing and a pie, using a backup crust.

entries.title: Fridge purge before the long weekend
entries.body: This morning before I left, I cleaned out the fridge so I wouldn't come home to something growing. Found two containers of the lentil soup I swore I'd eat, half a bag of spinach that had turned into spinach soup on its own, and a takeout container of pad see ew from what I'm pretty sure was last Thursday. All of it went in the trash. That's maybe ten dollars of food I threw away, which I'm now going to have to put in my sad little spreadsheet. Took out the trash and the recycling, watered the one plant I haven't killed, and set the thermostat down. Also finally grabbed the bag of clothes for donation from the hallway and put it in the trunk. It is now going to live in the trunk instead of the hallway, which is progress, technically.
entries.highlight: Cleared out spoiled food from the fridge before traveling and moved the donation bag to the car.

entries.title: Run-walk around my parents' block
entries.body: Woke up at my parents' feeling like a stuffed pillow after two days of leftovers. Went for a run around their neighborhood at 8 before the train home. It was 34 degrees and I wore Dad's old windbreaker, which smells like his garage. I lasted maybe six minutes of running before I had to walk, and then I did run one, walk one for the rest of the half hour. My lungs felt like they were full of cold sand. A guy walking a golden retriever passed me during one of my walking parts, which was humbling. Still, I was out the door, and that's more than I've done in about a month. Dad asked how far I went and I said thirty minutes, because that sounds better than saying I don't actually know. Train home at 11:15.
entries.highlight: Did a slow 30-minute run-walk around their parents' neighborhood after Thanksgiving.

entries.title: Alex and the oat latte walk
entries.body: Met Alex for coffee at 7:20 before the train, which is a very adult thing to do and I felt very adult doing it. Alex got an oat latte and I got a regular drip because I refuse to pay six dollars for coffee on a Monday. We walked around the block twice because neither of us wanted to go to work. Alex is thinking about asking for a promotion and was practicing how to say it, and I realized I've never once practiced how to ask for anything at work. I just kind of wait and hope somebody notices. Alex said that's not a strategy, that's a wish. Annoyingly true. I made the 8:05 with two minutes to spare. We said we'd do this every couple of weeks. I'm putting it in my calendar so it actually happens.
entries.favorite: That's not a strategy, that's a wish
entries.highlight: Had early coffee with friend Alex, who pointed out that waiting to be noticed at work isn't a strategy.

entries.title: Post office line out the door
entries.body: Saturday errand loop. First the post office to return a sweater that looked great online and terrible on me. The line was out the door because apparently everyone in the city is mailing holiday gifts today. I waited 35 minutes behind a man shipping what sounded like a box of loose bells. Then the pharmacy to refill my allergy prescription, which was ready, which never happens. Then the hardware store for a new shower curtain liner, because the old one has reached a color I would describe as concerning. Three things crossed off the list by noon. I celebrated with a bagel, which cost $4.75 and is going in the spreadsheet under everything else. Spent the afternoon on the couch with a blanket watching it get dark at 4:30. Productive day, frankly.
entries.favorite: Three things crossed off by noon
entries.highlight: Ran Saturday errands to the post office, pharmacy, and hardware store and finished by noon.

entries.title: Went for onions, came back without onions
entries.body: Did the weekly grocery run after coffee. The whole reason I went was onions, because I wanted to make the chili recipe Mom sent me. Got coffee, tofu, rice, frozen dumplings, a bag of clementines, and a fancy hot sauce that was on sale. Spent $58. Got home, unpacked, and realized there were no onions anywhere in the bags. I stood in my kitchen holding a clementine like it had betrayed me. Did not go back out because it was 28 degrees and I was already in socks. So no chili. Made the frozen dumplings instead with the fancy hot sauce, which was frankly great. Next week I'm writing an actual list on my phone, and onions are going at the very top, in capital letters.
entries.highlight: Went grocery shopping specifically for onions, forgot the onions, and made frozen dumplings instead.

entries.title: Dad called about the knee
entries.body: Dad called me tonight, which never happens. Usually Mom calls and passes the phone to him for a minute. He wanted to know if I'd watched the game, which I hadn't, and then he admitted the real reason: his doctor wants him to try physical therapy for his knee and he doesn't want to. He thinks it's a waste of time and that the knee is just old. I told him the knee is the same age as the rest of him and the rest of him is fine. He laughed, which I count as a win. He said he'll think about it, which in Dad language means maybe next year. We talked for twenty minutes about nothing much after that, mostly his theory about why the neighbor's inflatable snowman keeps falling over. I liked that he called me.
entries.highlight: Got a rare call from Dad, who is resisting physical therapy for his knee.

entries.title: Autopay for the electric bill, finally
entries.body: Paid rent tonight, $1,650 like always, plus the internet bill and the electric bill. The electric bill was $96 because my radiator is basically on all the time and the windows in this apartment are more of a suggestion than a barrier. I finally set up autopay for electric so I stop getting the little late reminder email every month. It took eleven minutes. I have been avoiding an eleven minute task for about two years. Put everything in the spreadsheet too. I'm seeing a pattern where the fixed stuff is fine and the problem is the everything else column, which is basically one big takeout receipt. Small goal for the rest of December: no lunch purchases more than twice a week. I'm writing that down here so I can't pretend I didn't say it.
entries.favorite: Eleven minutes, two years of avoiding it
entries.highlight: Paid rent and bills, set up autopay for electricity, and set a goal to buy lunch at most twice a week.

entries.title: First spin class, front row by accident
entries.body: Went to my first spin class at the gym this morning, the 10am Sunday one. I've had a membership for eight months and have used it maybe ten times, so this felt overdue. I got there late and the only bike open was in the front row, right in front of the instructor, Tamsin, who is about five feet tall and has the lungs of a drill sergeant. She kept saying add a quarter turn and I kept pretending to add a quarter turn. Forty-five minutes. I sweated through my shirt in about eight. My legs are going to hurt tomorrow, I can already tell, especially on the stairs at the train. But I felt strong in a way I haven't in a while, kind of buzzing all afternoon. I'm going back Thursday, and I'm picking a bike in the back row.
entries.favorite: Pretending to add a quarter turn
entries.highlight: Took a first spin class at the gym, ended up in the front row, and felt strong afterwards.

entries.title: 1:1 with Dana about bug triage
entries.body: Had a 1:1 with Dana this afternoon. We were supposed to talk about my projects, but it turned into twenty minutes about bug triage, because the queue is out of control and the design bugs keep getting tagged as low priority. We figured out a plan pretty quickly: I'll do a weekly sweep on Tuesdays and flag the ones that actually hurt users. Useful, fine. But I left feeling a little invisible, if I'm being real. I redesigned the settings page this fall and nobody has mentioned it once, and I didn't bring it up either, because it felt like bragging. Dana did say I'm reliable, which is nice, but reliable is also what people say about a dishwasher. Ate lunch at my desk again. Leftover dumplings, cold. I'm not in a great mood about work this week.
entries.highlight: Had a 1:1 with manager Dana about bug triage but felt their bigger design work was going unnoticed.

entries.title: Back row bike, round two
entries.body: Spin class number two, Thursday at 6:30 after work. I actually went, which surprised me, because it was dark and sleeting and the couch was making a very persuasive argument. Got a bike in the back row this time, near the fan. Tamsin still saw me and still told me to add a quarter turn, so the back row isn't the hiding spot I'd hoped. My legs were still a little sore from Sunday, but by the second song it felt fine. I felt stronger than last time, like I could actually breathe during the hills instead of just gasping. Afterward I walked home in the sleet and didn't even mind it. Made scrambled eggs and toast for dinner instead of ordering anything. That's two good decisions in one evening, which might be my record.
entries.highlight: Went to a second spin class after work despite sleet, felt stronger, and cooked dinner afterward.

entries.title: The trunk donation bag is gone
entries.body: The bag of clothes that moved from my hallway to my trunk before Thanksgiving has finally left my life. Drove it to the donation center this morning, along with a second bag I filled last night: three sweaters I never wear, a pair of jeans from 2019, and a toaster that only toasts one side. The guy at the drop-off took it all without even looking, which felt anticlimactic after a month of buildup. Then I went to the hardware store, got a new doormat, and swept the hallway. The hallway looks huge now. It's not, it's still about four feet wide, but it looks huge to me. Crossed three things off the list before noon again. I'm starting to think Sunday mornings are my productive time and I should stop wasting them sleeping.
entries.highlight: Finally dropped off two bags of donations that had been sitting in the car for a month.

entries.title: Quarterly metrics in an empty office
entries.body: The office was about a third full today because everybody is already on vacation, and I loved it. Blocked off the whole morning for the quarterly metrics write-up and, for once, actually kept the block. Turned off Slack from 9 to 11:30. Nobody even noticed. Got a full draft done before lunch, with charts showing the new settings page cut support tickets by eighteen percent. Eighteen percent. I sent it to Dana and she replied with a thumbs up emoji, which I am choosing to interpret generously. Marcus was in too and we ate lunch in the actual kitchen area instead of at our desks, because there was nobody to impress by looking busy. He told me about his in-laws visiting for a week. Left at 5:15. Quiet weeks are underrated.
entries.highlight: Used a quiet pre-holiday office to finish the quarterly metrics draft, showing their redesign reduced support tickets.

entries.title: Christmas cards with Dad until midnight
entries.body: Christmas at my parents'. I took the train up yesterday afternoon and it was packed with people holding pie boxes, so I fit right in. Mom made her usual feast: the ham, the scalloped potatoes, the green beans she insists on making with crispy onions from a can. I gave Mom new gardening gloves and a seed catalog with the pages I thought she'd like folded down, and she immediately started circling things. Dad got a heated blanket for his knee, which he pretended not to love and then used all evening. They gave me a cast iron pan, which feels like a message about my takeout habits. After dinner we played gin rummy until midnight. Dad won four games and gloated about every single one. My stomach hurts and I'm very happy.
entries.highlight: Spent Christmas at their parents' with a big dinner, exchanged gifts including a cast iron pan, and played cards until midnight.

entries.title: Skipped the Christmas morning run
entries.body: Writing this one late, after the cards. This morning I had the very ambitious plan to go for a run before presents, to make room for the ham. I laced up my shoes, opened the front door, felt the 19 degree air hit my face, and closed the front door. Went back to my old bedroom and slept until 9:30. Frankly, I needed it. This past month has been a lot of late nights, and my body was pretty clearly telling me to slow down. I've been getting maybe six hours on weeknights, and I could feel it in my head all of last week. I woke up actually rested, which felt like a present on its own. Mom had coffee ready. No guilt about the run. Okay, a little guilt. But mostly not.
entries.highlight: Skipped a planned Christmas morning run in the cold and slept in, feeling rested for the first time in weeks.

entries.title: Interview feedback on the 26th
entries.body: Took the 9:10 train home from my parents' and worked from my kitchen table in the afternoon. I owed interview feedback for two design candidates from last week, and I've been putting it off because writing feedback makes me feel like a judge on a cooking show. Turned off Slack for two hours and just wrote it. One candidate was clearly great, one had a beautiful portfolio but couldn't explain any of her decisions. I tried to be fair and specific instead of just saying good energy. Got both done before 3. Then I spent an embarrassing amount of time seasoning the new cast iron pan, following a video. Shut the laptop at 5:30. Ate leftover ham from the container Mom forced on me. Good transition day back to real life.
entries.highlight: Worked from home after the holiday, wrote overdue interview feedback, and seasoned a new cast iron pan.

entries.title: New year goals: four of them
entries.body: New Year's Day. Wrote my goals down on an index card and stuck it to the fridge with the pizza place magnet, which feels ironic. One: run a 5K. Not fast, just the whole thing without stopping. Two: cook more, meaning actually use the cast iron pan for more than eggs. Three: save more, specifically enough to move out of this dark apartment by the end of the year. Four: stop eating lunch at my desk. That last one sounds tiny but I eat lunch at my desk probably four days out of five, and I think it's making me a worse, crankier person. I also thought about a work goal, but I didn't know how to phrase it. Something like be noticed, but that sounds sad on an index card. Maybe I'll figure that one out later.
entries.highlight: Wrote four New Year's goals: run a 5K, cook more, save to move apartments, and stop eating lunch at their desk.

entries.title: All-hands and someone else's applause
entries.body: First day back. Started with the all-hands, which ran 25 minutes long because the CEO did a whole year in review slideshow. One slide was about the new checkout flow and how it boosted conversion, and they thanked Marcus's engineering team by name. Which, great, they built it. But I designed it. I spent six weeks on that flow. Nobody said the word design once. I sat there clapping like an idiot. Then back-to-back calls until 1, so I ate lunch at my desk again. Day two of the year and goal number four is already broken. Marcus messaged me afterward and said that slide should have had your name on it. That helped a little. I don't know what to do with this feeling except write it down here, so here it is.
entries.highlight: Felt overlooked when the checkout flow they designed was credited only to engineering at the all-hands.

entries.title: Onboarding spec due at 8pm
entries.body: Stayed late to finish the onboarding spec before the deadline, which was technically end of day and practically 8pm, when Elena needed it to prep for her product review. The spec covers the first three screens new users see, and the current flow is frankly a mess, seven steps where three would do. I had a lot of opinions and not a lot of time. Ordered pad thai to my desk at 6:30 and ate it over my keyboard. Got it in at 7:45, fifteen minutes early, which I'm weirdly proud of. Elena replied this is exactly what I needed, which felt really good after last week. The office at night is creepy, though. The motion lights kept turning off on me because I wasn't moving enough. Got home at 9. Bed.
entries.favorite: Elena saying exactly what I needed
entries.highlight: Worked late to finish the onboarding spec for product manager Elena and got appreciative feedback.

entries.title: Yoga with the resolution crowd
entries.body: Went to the 6pm yoga class after work. The gym was absolutely packed, January resolution energy everywhere, people wandering around holding brand new water bottles like they'd just been handed a baby. I am one of them, I know. The class was called gentle flow, which was a lie. My hamstrings are apparently made of guitar strings. The instructor kept saying breathe into your hips and I have no idea how to do that. But by the end, lying on the mat in the dark, I felt the most relaxed I have since vacation. I found muscles in my hips tonight that I'm pretty sure weren't there before January. Walked home and made eggs in the cast iron. Two days of exercise in one week. Index card is still on the fridge, judging me less.
entries.favorite: Lying on the mat in the dark
entries.highlight: Went to a crowded January yoga class, found it harder than expected, and felt relaxed afterward.

entries.title: I made a list and still forgot
entries.body: Sunday grocery run after coffee. This time I made an actual list on my phone, like I promised myself after the onion incident. Onions were on it. I got the onions. Victory. Also got pasta, a jar of pesto, parmesan, chicken thighs, spinach, eggs, oat milk, and bananas. $67. Got home, unpacked everything, and realized I forgot dish soap, which was not on the list because I didn't know I was out until I went to wash the pan tonight. Washed the cast iron with just hot water, which I think you're supposed to do anyway, so maybe that was fate. Lesson learned: check the cabinet before making the list, not just the fridge. It's still progress. The list worked for everything that was actually on it.
entries.highlight: Used a written grocery list for the first time, got everything on it, but forgot dish soap.

entries.title: Pesto pasta with a podcast
entries.body: Tried a new recipe tonight: pasta with pesto, chicken, and spinach. Okay, new recipe is generous, since the pesto came out of a jar. But I cooked the chicken thighs in the cast iron and they got a real crust on them, and I wilted the spinach in at the end, and it tasted like something you'd pay seventeen dollars for. Listened to a podcast about the history of the shipping container while cooking, which is the kind of thing I find relaxing now, apparently. Whole thing took 30 minutes. I made a double batch on purpose so I can bring it for lunch the next few days. I'm calling this the start of goal number two. Will definitely make it again. Maybe next time I'll even try making the pesto myself. Maybe.
entries.highlight: Cooked pesto pasta with chicken in the new cast iron pan and made extra for lunches.

entries.title: Three days of not buying lunch
entries.body: Small but real: it's Wednesday and I haven't bought lunch once this week. I portioned out the pesto pasta on Monday night into three containers and they've lasted exactly through today. Tonight I did a mini meal prep for Thursday and Friday too, roasting a tray of chicken and broccoli and making a pot of rice. Took about an hour and a half with the podcast on. Weekday me will be grateful. I did a quick calculation and three homemade lunches cost me about eleven dollars total, versus around thirty-five if I'd gone downstairs. I'm still eating at my desk, though. Baby steps. One goal at a time. The pan is getting a nice dark color now, which I'm told is good. Mom texted asking if I'd used it yet and I sent her a photo.
entries.highlight: Went three workdays without buying lunch by meal prepping, saving about $24.

entries.title: The 6:15 yoga class exists
entries.body: Did the 6:15am yoga class before work. I didn't know human beings were awake and flexible at 6:15am, but there were eleven of them, and most looked like they'd been doing this for years. One woman brought her own blanket and a little eye pillow. I was in leggings with a hole in the knee. I felt slow and stiff the whole time, especially in anything that involved balancing on one foot. But the weird thing is I was more awake than usual all morning. I didn't even get my usual 10am headache. I caught the 8:05 with time to spare and finished two design reviews before standup. I don't think I'm a morning person now, let's not get crazy. But I might be a Friday morning person. We'll see.
entries.highlight: Tried an early morning yoga class before work and felt more awake all morning.

entries.title: Holiday Monday, did absolutely nothing
entries.body: Day off for the holiday. My plan was a run in the morning, then laundry, then maybe a new recipe. What actually happened: I slept until 9, read on the couch until noon, took a nap at 3, and went to bed at 9:30. I skipped the workout entirely. I felt guilty about it for about an hour and then I stopped, because I was running on fumes and I knew it. This month has already had a deadline night, a lot of meetings, and the all-hands thing still rattling around in my head. I did make soup, so I guess I'm not a total loss. Tomorrow back to normal. But I think I needed one day with nothing on the list, and I'm going to try not to apologize for it.
entries.highlight: Spent a holiday Monday resting instead of exercising and decided not to feel guilty about it.

entries.title: The radiator that sounds like a drum kit
entries.body: My radiator has started making a noise at 5am that sounds like someone hitting a pipe with a wrench. It's been happening for a week, and it's been waking me up a solid hour before my alarm. Finally emailed the super, Gus, who answered within ten minutes, which I did not expect. He came by tonight at 7, bled the valve, and told me the building is old and I should expect some character. Character. He also told me my window is letting in so much cold air that he could feel it from the door, and taped a strip of foam on it for me. It's nice to have a fix that cost zero dollars. But it also made me look around and think, I really do want to live somewhere less drafty. Moving fund, here I come.
entries.favorite: Gus fixing it in ten minutes
entries.highlight: Got the building super to fix a noisy radiator and drafty window, which renewed their wish to move.

entries.title: Metrics morning, Slack off
entries.body: Blocked off the morning for the quarterly metrics review deck and actually kept it, two months in a row now. Turned off Slack for two hours and set my status to heads down, which felt rebellious. Elena asked me a question in person instead, which was fair. I got a full draft done before lunch. This time I added a slide specifically about design impact, with the settings page and the checkout flow, and the numbers for both. I don't know if anybody will read it, but after the all-hands I decided if nobody else says it, I'll say it myself, quietly, on slide seven. Then I left right at 5:30 and went to the grocery store on the way home. I'm a little nervous about slide seven, to be fair. It feels like raising my hand.
entries.highlight: Finished the quarterly metrics deck during protected focus time and added a slide highlighting design's impact.

entries.title: Laundromat Sunday in the snow
entries.body: It snowed about four inches overnight, the first real snow of the winter, and of course it's laundry day. My building doesn't have laundry, so every other Sunday I drag a giant blue bag three blocks to the laundromat. Did that through the snow this morning, slipping a little on the corner by the bakery. The laundromat was cozy, though, warm and smelling like dryer sheets. I read for an hour while everything dried. Then I stopped at the hardware store for ice melt for my front steps and a new scraper for the car. On the way home some kids had built a snowman with a traffic cone for a hat. I took a picture for Mom. If I ever move, in-unit laundry is going on the list, right at the top.
entries.highlight: Hauled laundry to the laundromat through the first big snow of winter and picked up ice melt.

entries.title: Canceled the streaming service I forgot
entries.body: Paid rent and the bills tonight. While I was going through my bank statement, line by line like a detective, I found a streaming service I signed up for to watch one show last summer. $15.99 a month. For six months. That's ninety-six dollars I paid to not watch anything. Canceled it immediately. The cancel button was hidden behind four screens asking if I was sure, which was insulting. I also noticed I've been paying for two cloud storage plans, so I canceled the smaller one. That's about twenty dollars a month back. I put it straight into a savings account I'm starting to think of as the moving fund. It only has $340 in it, but it has a name now, and that makes it feel real.
entries.highlight: Found and canceled two forgotten subscriptions and moved the savings into a new moving fund.

entries.title: Mom's chili, with onions this time
entries.body: Finally made Mom's chili, two months after the great onion failure. I had onions. I had everything. Browned the beef in the cast iron, added the beans and tomatoes and her spice mix, which is mostly cumin and something she calls a pinch of love that I think is actually brown sugar. Let it simmer for an hour while I listened to a podcast and wiped down the counters. It turned out better than expected. Not as good as hers, but close. Enough leftovers for two days of lunch, maybe three. I texted Mom a photo and she replied it needs more cumin, which she cannot possibly know from a photo. I'm adding more cumin next time anyway. The apartment smells amazing and it's 22 degrees outside. Perfect night for it.
entries.highlight: Successfully made Mom's chili recipe for the first time, with leftovers for lunches.

entries.title: Stuck to the list for once
entries.body: Went to the grocery store at 8:30 before it got busy, which turns out to be the secret. Nobody there but me and two older guys debating the best bananas. I checked the cabinet before making the list this time, like I promised myself. Got spinach, bananas, eggs, tomatoes, a big bag of rice, black beans, chicken thighs, dish soap, and more cumin for the chili. Stuck to the list for once. I didn't buy a single thing that wasn't on it, not even the fancy cookies by the register that always get me. $61. In and out in 25 minutes. I walked out feeling weirdly proud, like a person who has their life together, which I very much do not, but for 25 minutes I was that person. Same plan next week.
entries.highlight: Shopped early, checked the pantry first, and stuck to the grocery list completely for $61.

entries.title: Annual review: raise and a challenge
entries.body: Annual review today with Dana. I was nervous all morning and ate half a granola bar for breakfast. It went well. Better than well. I got a raise, four and a half percent, which is more than I expected. And she brought up the metrics deck, specifically slide seven, and said it was exactly the kind of thing she wants to see more of. Her main feedback was that I should take on more ownership this year. She said I do great work on what I'm handed, but she wants me to pick a problem and own it, bring it to her instead of waiting. I said okay, and then on the train home I thought, I have no idea how to do that. But I'm going to figure it out. Slide seven worked. Raising my hand worked.
entries.highlight: Got a raise at the annual review and feedback from Dana to take on more ownership this year.

entries.title: Where the raise is going
entries.body: Did the monthly budget check-in tonight, with real numbers this time. Groceries came in under budget at $248 for the month, which is a first. Eating out was still too much at $290, but that's down from $412 in November, so the line is moving the right way. The raise kicks in on the next paycheck, and I decided before I can spend it that half of it goes straight to the moving fund automatically. Set up the transfer tonight. It'll add about $150 a month. If I keep that up plus what I'm already saving, I could have enough for a deposit and movers by late summer. I actually said that out loud to my empty kitchen. Late summer. That's a real date. It feels a little scary and a lot exciting.
entries.highlight: Reviewed the monthly budget, saw takeout spending dropping, and set half of the new raise to go to a moving fund.

entries.title: Valentine's Day on the late train
entries.body: Caught the 8:05 train, which showed up at 8:21, so I stood on the platform in the wind for sixteen extra minutes. I cleared my inbox down to four emails while I waited, so the wind was at least productive. The office had heart-shaped cookies in the kitchen from Elena, and Marcus ate three before 10. Spent the morning sketching ideas for something I could actually own, like Dana said. Right now the front-runner is our empty states, all those screens that say no data yet and look like a broken page. Nobody owns them. I wrote a one-page pitch. Haven't sent it yet. Ate lunch at my desk again, a cookie and some chili. Valentine's Day plans: laundry and a movie, which frankly sounds pretty romantic to me right now.
entries.favorite: Inbox down to four on the platform
entries.highlight: Used a late train to clear their inbox and drafted a pitch to take ownership of the product's empty states.

entries.title: The winter farmers market
entries.body: Found out the farmers market runs all winter inside the old armory building, so I walked over this morning. It's smaller than the summer one but cozy, with a guy playing the fiddle near the door. Bought a loaf of sourdough, a bag of potatoes, a dozen eggs from a farm whose chickens apparently all have names, frozen blueberries from last summer, and a jar of honey. Spent $38, which is more than the grocery store would charge, but the eggs have orange yolks and the honey guy gave me a sample of something called buckwheat honey that tasted like molasses. Made toast with the sourdough and honey for lunch. It felt like a small vacation. I think I'm going to make this a monthly thing, at least in winter, when I need a reason to leave the apartment.
entries.highlight: Discovered the indoor winter farmers market and bought bread, eggs, and honey.

entries.title: Tax documents in a shoebox
entries.body: Holiday Monday, so I finally tackled taxes, or at least the gathering part. My tax documents live in a shoebox under my bed, which is a system I would not recommend. Found my W-2, the interest statement from my savings account, which was a whole eleven dollars, and a receipt from 2022 for a lamp I don't even own anymore. I made a folder on my laptop and scanned everything in. Then I spent forty minutes on the tax website before realizing I'll probably get back around $600. I immediately thought about spending it and then immediately thought, no, moving fund. I don't recognize myself. I also threw out the shoebox and bought a real folder. Big day for adulthood. I rewarded myself with a long walk in the slush.
entries.highlight: Organized tax documents on a holiday Monday and planned to put an expected refund into the moving fund.

entries.title: Lunch break haircut counts as a lunch break
entries.body: Got a haircut on my lunch break at the place two blocks from the office. Technically this is the first lunch break all month where I left my desk, so I'm counting it toward goal number four, even though I didn't eat anything until 2. The barber, Nico, asked what I wanted and I said shorter, and he took that very seriously. It's a little shorter than usual, and my ears are cold now, but I feel like a new person. Marcus said I looked like I'd been promoted, which made me laugh. Cost $38 with tip. I wish I could explain why a haircut makes such a big difference in how I feel, but it does. It's like resetting a phone. Same phone, works better. Back to the desk for the afternoon.
entries.highlight: Got a lunch-break haircut, which doubled as their first time leaving the desk at lunch all month.

entries.title: Sheet-pan chicken, zero dishes
entries.body: Made sheet-pan chicken for dinner. The whole recipe is: chicken thighs, potatoes from the farmers market, a red onion, olive oil, salt, paprika, one pan, 425 degrees, forty minutes. I read it on the train home and thought, there's no way it's that easy. It's that easy. The potatoes got crispy on the bottom and the onions went sweet and a little burnt in the good way. It was frankly delicious, and the best part is I only had to wash one pan, which matters a lot when your sink is the size of a shoebox. Two lunches were packed before I even sat down to eat. I've now cooked dinner four nights this week, which might be a personal record since college. I'm starting to understand why people get into this. It's kind of calming.
entries.highlight: Made an easy sheet-pan chicken dinner and cooked at home four nights in one week.

entries.title: The empty states deck at 7:45pm
entries.body: Stayed late tonight to finish the slide deck for my empty states pitch. Dana said bring her a problem and own it, so I'm bringing her a problem. I went through the whole product and screenshotted every screen that shows up blank when a new user has no data. There are thirty-one of them. Thirty-one screens that basically say nothing here, good luck. Some of them don't even say that, they're just white. I put them all on one slide in a grid and it looks horrifying, which is the point. Ordered pho to my desk and got the deck done at 7:45. Sent it to Dana with a short note asking for twenty minutes this week. My heart was pounding when I hit send, which is ridiculous. It's a slide deck. But it's my slide deck.
entries.highlight: Stayed late to build a pitch deck on the product's thirty-one blank empty states and sent it to Dana.

entries.title: Bed at 9:30 after the deck night
entries.body: Was supposed to go to spin tonight, but after last night I was running on about five and a half hours of sleep and a lot of nervous energy about the pitch. Skipped the workout and went to bed at 9:30, which felt very old person, but I'm fine with it. Before that I took a hot shower, made some tea, and put my phone in the kitchen so I wouldn't check for a reply from Dana every four minutes. That was the hardest part. My body was filing complaints, kind of loudly. I had a headache since noon and my eyes felt sandy. I'm learning that late nights cost me two days, not one. That's not a great trade. Note to self: deadlines are going to happen, but maybe I could start decks earlier.
entries.highlight: Skipped a workout and went to bed early to recover from a late night at work.

entries.title: First time cooking salmon at home
entries.body: Cooked salmon at home for the first time ever. I've always been scared of it, partly because of the smell and partly because I assumed I'd ruin a twelve dollar piece of salmon. I did not ruin it. Salt, pepper, skin side down in the cast iron, four minutes, flip, two more minutes. The skin got crispy and Mom, who I texted a photo to, said it looked restaurant quality, which coming from her is basically a medal. Made rice and some frozen green beans on the side. I made an extra portion for Monday lunch, but I'm told salmon doesn't keep great, so we'll see. The apartment does smell like salmon now, so the windows are open even though it's 38 degrees. Worth it. Friday night dinner and I didn't order anything. Who am I.
entries.highlight: Cooked salmon at home for the first time and was proud of how it turned out.

entries.title: Ate lunch in the kitchen with Ravi
entries.body: I brought the sheet-pan chicken leftovers today, the third week in a row I've meal-prepped lunches. But the bigger thing is where I ate it. Ravi from the data team was heating up his lunch in the office kitchen at 12:30 and asked if I wanted to sit with him, and instead of saying I've got a thing, I said sure. We sat at the long table by the window for 35 minutes. He's training for a half marathon in May and runs at 6am, which I find both inspiring and frightening. He told me about some app that gets you from the couch to a 5K in nine weeks. That's goal number one, so I wrote the name down. It's the first time this year I've actually eaten a full lunch away from my desk. Tiny thing. Felt huge.
entries.favorite: Saying sure instead of I've got a thing
entries.highlight: Ate a home-cooked lunch away from the desk with coworker Ravi, who recommended a beginner running plan.

entries.title: Dana said yes to empty states
entries.body: Dana finally had twenty minutes on Friday and she said yes. The empty states project is mine. She wants a plan by the end of the month, with a rollout in three phases. She said, and I wrote this down right after, this is what ownership looks like. So today I blocked the whole morning, turned off Slack, and actually kept the block. Got a full draft of the plan done before lunch: which screens get fixed first, who I need from engineering, and how we'll measure if it worked. Marcus already agreed to help with the front end. I keep catching myself smiling at my laptop like a weirdo. It's not a huge project, to be fair. It's blank screens. But it's the first thing at this job I asked for instead of just being handed.
entries.favorite: This is what ownership looks like
entries.highlight: Got Dana's approval to own the empty states project and drafted the rollout plan during focus time.

entries.title: Car registration at the DMV
entries.body: Car registration was due Friday, so I took a long lunch and went to the DMV, because the online system rejected my payment three times for reasons it would not explain. The DMV was exactly what you'd imagine. I took a number, B47. They were serving B12. I sat between a teenager nervously studying for a permit test and a man eating sunflower seeds very loudly. An hour and twenty minutes later I had my sticker. $89. I barely drive the car, since I take the train everywhere, and I've started wondering if I even need it. But Mom and Dad are a train ride away, and having the car for the holidays and big grocery runs is nice. I'll think about it. Ate a granola bar on the way back. Not exactly a real lunch break.
entries.highlight: Spent a long lunch break at the DMV renewing their car registration for $89.

entries.title: Forty-minute walk on the first warm morning
entries.body: It was 52 degrees this morning, the first morning in months that didn't feel like an attack, so I went for a long walk before work. Did a loop down to the river and back, about forty minutes. I felt slow, especially on the hill back up, but I showed up, and the sun was coming up orange over the bridge, which almost made me late because I stopped to look at it. Got a coffee from the cart by the station and made the 8:05 with one minute to spare. I was actually useful in standup instead of just nodding. I keep noticing that moving in the morning makes the whole day better, and I keep not doing it. Maybe spring is the time to change that. I downloaded Ravi's running app tonight.
entries.favorite: The orange sunrise over the bridge
entries.highlight: Took a 40-minute walk on the first warm morning of spring and downloaded a beginner running app.

entries.title: Fourteen saved apartment listings
entries.body: Didn't do any real errands tonight. Instead I sat on the couch and started actually looking at apartment listings, which I've been avoiding because it makes me want to move tomorrow. Set my filters: one bedroom, in-unit laundry, under $1,950, close enough to a train that I can still make the 8:05. Saved fourteen listings. Six of them have photos so dark you can't tell what the rooms look like, which is suspicious. Two of them say cozy, which I've learned means tiny. One has a kitchen with an actual window over the sink and I may have stared at it for a full minute. My lease ends August 31st. The moving fund is at $1,420. It's not enough yet, but I can see it from here. I also emailed one landlord to ask about viewings in April.
entries.highlight: Started seriously browsing apartment listings, saved fourteen, and requested an April viewing.

entries.title: Spring closet purge, round two
entries.body: Spring clean-out today, partly because I'm thinking about moving and every object I own suddenly looks like something I'll have to carry down three flights of stairs. Went through the closet and filled two bags: winter coats I never wear, a lot of free t-shirts from events, and a sweater Mom knitted that I love but that is literally too small for me. That one I kept. Drove the bags to the donation center by 11 and was home by noon. Hallway looks huge again. Then I went through the kitchen drawer of mystery cords and threw out nine of them. Nine cords for devices I no longer own. Crossed three things off the list, had a sandwich on the fire escape, and felt like the apartment could breathe a little more. Lighter apartment, lighter move.
entries.highlight: Did a spring closet purge, donated two bags of clothes, and threw out nine old cords.

entries.title: Scratchy throat, skipped spin
entries.body: Woke up with a scratchy throat and spent all day hoping it was allergies. It's probably not allergies. Half the office has had a cold this week and Elena has been sneezing into her elbow in every meeting like a sad trumpet. I skipped spin tonight and went to bed at 9:30. Before that I made a big mug of tea with honey from the farmers market and ate toast for dinner, which is my sick food, a tradition from when Mom used to make me cinnamon toast when I stayed home from school. I really needed the sleep, cold or not. I've been sleeping badly since the clocks changed. I also put the running app's week one plan on pause, which is annoying, since I was finally going to start it this week. Message received, body.
entries.highlight: Felt a cold coming on, skipped spin class, and went to bed early.

entries.title: Full cold, worked from the couch
entries.body: Not allergies. It's a full cold now. Worked from home today because nobody wants me coughing on the 8:05. Did my two meetings with the camera off, which was a gift to everyone. Then I logged off at 3 and lay on the couch like a beached whale. Skipped the workout, obviously, and went to bed at 9:30 again. I made a pot of chicken soup with rice using the leftover chicken thighs, carrots, an onion, and a lot of garlic. It wasn't Mom's, but it was mine, and it worked. Last year I would have ordered soup from the diner for fourteen dollars and they'd forget the crackers. Mom called to check on me and told me to put Vicks on my feet, which I did not do, but I appreciated the thought. Sleep. Lots of it.
entries.highlight: Worked from home with a cold, made homemade chicken soup, and went to bed early.

entries.title: First apartment viewing: the cozy one
entries.body: Feeling mostly better, so I went to my first apartment viewing this afternoon. It was the one listing that responded, a one bedroom about ten minutes from the station. The listing said cozy. It was cozy in the way a closet is cozy. The bedroom fit a bed and nothing else, and the in-unit laundry was a single tiny machine under the kitchen counter that washes and dries in one, very slowly, according to the agent. There were eight other people at the viewing, all opening cabinets with serious expressions, which made me feel like I should be opening cabinets too. So I did. Very serious cabinet opening. I didn't apply. But it was good practice. Now I know what questions to ask, like how much natural light, and is the laundry real.
entries.highlight: Went to a first apartment viewing, which was too small, but learned what to look for.

entries.title: Week one, day one of the running plan
entries.body: Started the couch to 5K plan this morning, finally. Week one day one is: walk five minutes, then alternate one minute of running with a minute and a half of walking, for twenty minutes. The app has a cheerful voice that says start running now, like it's a fun surprise every time. Did it on the gym treadmill at 6:40 because it was raining. Ravi was there too, on his long run, doing about nine miles while I did my tiny intervals next to him. He gave me a thumbs up and I tried not to die in front of him. I felt slow but I showed up. Then I did a few of the weight machines afterwards, just to try them, mostly the leg press. I answered email on the train like someone who'd had three coffees, on one. Day two is Thursday.
entries.favorite: The app voice saying start running now
entries.highlight: Began a nine-week beginner running plan on the treadmill, working toward the year's 5K goal.

entries.title: Stir-fry with the last of the vegetables
entries.body: Made a stir-fry for dinner tonight with everything sad in the fridge: half a bell pepper, a lonely carrot, some broccoli, a little bit of cabbage, and the tofu I bought two weeks ago and kept forgetting. I pressed the tofu with a cookbook, which I learned from a video and felt very proud of. Cooked it in the cast iron in batches so it got crispy instead of soggy. The sauce was soy sauce, garlic, ginger, honey, and a little rice vinegar. It was frankly better than the takeout place down the street, and I'm not saying that to be nice to myself. Tomorrow's lunch is already in a container. Ran in the morning, cooked at night. I don't want to jinx it but I feel like a slightly more functional person today.
entries.highlight: Made a stir-fry from leftover vegetables and crispy tofu that beat their usual takeout.

entries.title: Trivia night with Sam: fourth place
entries.body: Sam dragged me to trivia night at a bar near Sam's apartment. Our team name was The Index Cards, after my goals card, which Sam thinks is hilarious. It was just the two of us against teams of six. We came in fourth out of eleven, which feels like first when you're outnumbered. We crushed the geography round and completely died on the sports round. I knew one sports answer and it was a guess. The final question was about the longest river in Asia and we got it, and Sam stood up and cheered like we'd won the lottery. We laughed so hard about how bad we were at the music round that the bartender gave us free fries. Got home at 11, which is late for a Wednesday, but I don't regret it. We're going back next month.
entries.highlight: Went to trivia night with friend Sam as a two-person team and placed fourth out of eleven.

entries.title: Back on the bike with Tamsin
entries.body: Went back to Saturday spin this morning, the 9am class, after basically taking all of March off. Tamsin, the tiny loud instructor, saw me walk in and said look who's back, in front of the whole class. Nowhere to hide. The playlist was all 2000s pop and somehow that made the hills easier. My legs were still a little stiff from the running intervals this week, and the train station stairs will have something to say on Monday, but it felt good to be back. I've noticed that I'm much better at exercise when it's on the calendar like a meeting. The days I just think I'll go later, I don't go. So I booked the next two Saturdays in the app. I slept better afterwards, too. Took a two-hour nap this afternoon, which may or may not count as sleeping better.
entries.highlight: Returned to Saturday spin class after a month off and booked the next two classes.

entries.title: Washed the windows for the first time
entries.body: After spin and before the nap, I did spring cleaning. Vacuumed everywhere, including under the couch, where I found a sock, a pen, and a fortune cookie fortune that said you will soon be surrounded by light. I took that personally, considering the whole reason I want to move is the lack of light. Then I washed the windows, inside and out, as far as I could reach without falling off the fire escape. I have never washed these windows. Ever. In three years. The difference is frankly embarrassing. The apartment is about thirty percent brighter, which maybe means it was never this dark, it was just this dirty. I'm still moving, but I'm going to feel a little guilty about it now. The apartment feels so much better. I opened every window for an hour.
entries.highlight: Did spring cleaning, washed the windows for the first time in three years, and the apartment got noticeably brighter.

entries.title: Mom's basement seedlings
entries.body: Called Mom on the walk home from the station. It's light out until almost 7:30 now, which makes walking and talking much nicer. Mom has forty-two seedlings growing under lights in the basement: tomatoes, peppers, and the zinnias she does every year. She named the grow light setup the nursery and says Dad is not allowed in there because he knocked over a tray in 2019 and has never been forgiven. Dad's knee is about the same. He still won't do physical therapy, and Mom has stopped bringing it up because it makes him grumpy. I told her about the apartment search and the cozy closet place, and she laughed so hard she had to put the phone down. We talked for over an hour. She wants me to come up for Mother's Day and help plant. I said yes.
entries.favorite: The nursery Dad is banned from
entries.highlight: Had a long call with Mom about her forty-two seedlings, Dad's knee, and the apartment search.

entries.title: Running plan rest day, actually resting
entries.body: Today was a planned rest day on the running plan. That's a new idea for me, a rest day that's in the plan, instead of a rest day that's just me not doing anything. I've done three runs so far. My calves are tight and my shins have an opinion about the sidewalk. So I followed the plan. No workout. Made pasta, stretched on the floor for fifteen minutes while watching a show, and went to bed at 9:30. My body was telling me to slow down, but in a normal way this time, not in a sick, burned out way. The app said rest is when you get stronger, which sounds like something on a poster in a dentist's office, but okay, I'll take it. Out cold by ten. Run four is Thursday.
entries.favorite: A rest day that's in the plan
entries.highlight: Took a scheduled rest day in the running plan after three runs and stretched before bed.

entries.title: Run four did not happen
entries.body: Run four was supposed to happen tonight. It did not happen. Work ran late because the empty states phase one review got moved to 4:30, and it went until 6, and by the time I got home it was dark and raining and I had a pile of dishes looking at me. So I skipped the workout and went to bed early. I'm writing this down anyway because I don't want to pretend I'm doing great when I'm doing medium. The pattern is clear, though. When I plan to work out after work, work wins. When I plan to work out in the morning, I win. I'm moving the running days to mornings starting next week. Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday, before the train. That's the deal. The review went well, by the way. Phase one is approved.
entries.highlight: Missed a planned run due to a late review, realized morning workouts work better, and got phase one of the project approved.

entries.title: Nico and the second haircut
entries.body: Haircut on my lunch break again, two months after the last one. Nico remembered me, which shouldn't feel as nice as it did. He asked how the shorter cut worked out and I said my ears were cold until March, and he said that's the price of looking good. Asked for the same cut, a little shorter, because it's spring and I'm committing to the look. $38 with tip again. Then I grabbed a sandwich from the deli next door and ate it on a bench in the little plaza by the office, outside, in the sun, which might be the first outdoor lunch of the year. People were out everywhere with their faces pointed up like plants. I sat there for twenty minutes. Should do this more, both the haircut and the bench.
entries.highlight: Got a lunch-break haircut and ate lunch outside in the sun for the first time this year.

entries.title: Viewing number two: the basement one
entries.body: Second apartment viewing tonight after work. The listing said garden level, which I now know means basement. The photos were taken with a very wide lens and a lot of lamps. In person, the windows were at sidewalk height, so the main view was people's ankles walking by and, at one point, a dog sniffing the glass. To be fair, it had in-unit laundry, a real one, and the kitchen was nice. But I'd be trading one dark apartment for a darker apartment, and the whole point of this is light. The landlord was friendly and offered me a cup of coffee, which made it awkward to say no. I said I'd think about it. I won't. Walked home through the park. The trees are starting to bud. Two down. Moving fund at $1,780.
entries.highlight: Toured a second apartment, which was a dark basement unit, and decided to keep looking.

entries.title: Week three intervals in the park
entries.body: Did my first outdoor run on the plan this morning, week three, day one. Ninety seconds of running, two minutes of walking, repeat. Went to the park at 8 on a Saturday, which is apparently when every runner in the city is out, plus about a hundred dogs. Everyone passing me looked like they'd been doing this for years. But I noticed something: the ninety seconds felt shorter than the one minute did two weeks ago. I could talk to myself during it, out loud, which got me a look from a man with a stroller. My face was stop-sign red the whole time, according to my reflection in a parked car. I felt strong today, though, actually strong. I made it through every interval, and I didn't cheat on any of them. Mornings work.
entries.highlight: Completed a first outdoor run in week three of the running plan and felt stronger than two weeks earlier.

entries.title: Fixed the drippy faucet myself
entries.body: The bathroom faucet has been dripping for about a month, a steady drip every two seconds that I could hear from bed. Instead of emailing Gus, I watched a video at lunch and decided to fix it myself. I don't know why. Spring confidence, maybe. Turned off the water under the sink, took the handle apart, found a small rubber washer that looked like it had been chewed, and took it to the hardware store in a sandwich bag so I could match it. The guy at the store said these are a dollar and twenty-nine cents, you'll be fine. I was fine. Took me forty minutes and I only dropped one screw down the drain, which I then rescued with a chopstick. The drip is gone. I keep going in there to look at it not dripping.
entries.favorite: Rescuing the screw with a chopstick
entries.highlight: Fixed a dripping bathroom faucet themselves with a $1.29 washer and a how-to video.

entries.title: The renewal letter says $1,725
entries.body: Paid rent tonight, and there was a letter under my door from the management company. My lease renewal offer. Rent is going up to $1,725 in September. That's $75 more a month for the same dark apartment with the radiator that sounds like a drum kit and the laundromat three blocks away. I sat with it for a while. Then I opened my spreadsheet and did the math, and the apartments I've been saving have been around $1,850 to $1,900. So the gap between staying and leaving just got smaller. I'm not renewing. I'm going to write the email tomorrow, when I'm calm, but I already know. This is the push I needed. I also set up autopay for the internet bill tonight, so at least one bill will stop surprising me.
entries.highlight: Received a lease renewal with a $75 rent increase and decided not to renew, committing to the move.

entries.title: Moving fund passes $2,000
entries.body: Sunday budget check-in with coffee. Groceries were $231 for April, the lowest yet, mostly because I've been meal prepping pretty much every week now. Eating out was $214, which is still too much, but it's about half of November. The moving fund officially passed $2,000 this week, $2,060 to be exact, thanks to the tax refund and the automatic transfer from the raise. I made a little chart in the spreadsheet with a line for where I need to be by August and a line for where I am. My line is a tiny bit behind. If I skip one dinner out a week, I'll catch up by July. I emailed the management company yesterday to say I'm not renewing. So now there's a deadline. Scary. Good scary.
entries.highlight: Reviewed the monthly budget, saw the moving fund pass $2,000, and confirmed they won't renew the lease.

entries.title: Alex got the promotion
entries.body: Met Alex for dinner at the Thai place downtown to celebrate, because Alex got the promotion. The one Alex was practicing how to ask for on our walk back in December. Alex said the trick was asking clearly, with a list of reasons, and then just sitting there in the silence. I told Alex about the empty states project and how I basically did the same thing with Dana. We clinked our Thai iced teas like they were champagne. We got the giggles about the time Alex locked us out of the dorm in a towel that I nearly choked on a noodle. Stayed until they closed and the server started turning chairs upside down around us. I spent $42, which I'm counting as a celebration expense, not an eating out expense. That's a category now. I just made it up.
entries.highlight: Celebrated friend Alex's promotion over a long dinner, comparing notes on asking for what they want at work.

entries.title: Chloe's second week, my first question
entries.body: The 8:05 showed up at 8:20, so I cleared my inbox on the platform and got to the office just in time for retro. During retro, the new junior designer, Chloe, who started last week, asked a really good question about why our buttons have four slightly different shades of blue. Nobody had an answer, including me, and I've been here three years. After the meeting she came by my desk and asked if I had a few minutes to walk her through the component library. I said sure and we spent forty-five minutes going through it. She takes notes in a little paper notebook, which I love. I realized halfway through that I know a lot more than I give myself credit for. Ate lunch at my desk again, but I was helping someone, so I'm allowing it.
entries.highlight: Helped new junior designer Chloe learn the component library and realized how much they know.

entries.title: Mother's Day planting the tomatoes
entries.body: Took the early train to my parents' for Mother's Day and spent the whole afternoon in the garden with Mom. We planted the tomatoes from her basement nursery, all twelve of them, plus peppers and a row of zinnias. Mom is very particular. Each tomato goes in deep, sideways, with a handful of crushed eggshells, and if you do it wrong she says hmm and redoes it next to you. Dad sat in a lawn chair at the edge of the garden supervising because his knee doesn't like kneeling. He was mostly supervising the sports radio. I brought Mom a hanging basket of fuchsias and she hung it right by the back door. Dirt caked on my hands, sunburned neck, eggshells in my pocket somehow. Took the 6pm train home. One of the best days in a while.
entries.favorite: Mom saying hmm and redoing my tomato
entries.highlight: Spent Mother's Day at their parents' house planting tomatoes and flowers with Mom while Dad supervised.

entries.title: Flannel sheets out, cotton sheets in
entries.body: Worked from home this morning, so before my first call I did the seasonal sheet swap. Flannel sheets off, cotton sheets on. I've been sleeping hot for two weeks and kept blaming the radiator, which, to be fair, is still somehow on even though it's May. Washed the flannel ones at the laundromat at lunch, because I had a gap between meetings, and folded them into the closet for October. Also took out three weeks of recycling, which was mostly cardboard boxes from online orders and oat milk cartons. The bedroom feels about five degrees cooler already. It's funny how changing the sheets makes a whole room feel new. I did my run before all this, too, week four, three minutes of running at a time. I was very efficient today. I'd like to be this person every Tuesday.
entries.highlight: Did the seasonal sheet swap and caught up on chores during a work-from-home morning.

entries.title: Physical results came back normal
entries.body: My annual physical was Thursday and the bloodwork results showed up in the patient portal this morning. Everything looks normal. Cholesterol is fine, vitamin D is a little low, which the doctor says is basically everyone who lives here and works indoors. She told me to keep up the exercise and get more sun. When I told her about the running plan she asked how far I'm running and I said about twelve minutes, and she said that counts, which was nice of her. She also asked about sleep and I said I'm working on it, and she said that's what everyone says. Fair. I sat on the steps outside my building this morning drinking coffee in the sun, technically following doctor's orders. Picked up vitamin D at the pharmacy. $9.
entries.highlight: Got normal results from the annual physical, with a doctor's suggestion to keep exercising and get more sun.

entries.title: Switched to a high-yield savings account
entries.body: Moved the moving fund into a high-yield savings account tonight. Ravi was talking about it at lunch last week, saying a regular savings account is basically a shoebox with a logo on it. My current one was paying almost nothing, which explains the eleven dollars of interest on my taxes. The new one pays a little over four percent. It took about twenty minutes to set up and another two days for the transfer. On $2,300, that's maybe eight dollars a month, which isn't going to change my life, but it's eight dollars for doing nothing, and that feels like a cheat code. Also moved some money from checking into savings, $200, because I didn't eat out at all last week. That's two money things in one night. I feel like an accountant, but a happy one.
entries.highlight: Moved the moving fund into a high-yield savings account and added $200 saved from not eating out.

entries.title: Measuring everything I own
entries.body: Worked from home today and spent my lunch break measuring all my furniture with a tape measure, because the next apartment viewings are coming up and I want to know what fits. Couch: 84 inches. Bed: queen, obviously. Dresser: 52 inches, and so heavy I'm not sure it's worth moving. Bookshelf: tall, wobbly, held together by hope. I wrote it all on a note in my phone. Then I vacuumed, because I was down there on the floor anyway, and took out the recycling. While measuring, I realized I probably don't want to bring half of this. The dresser I got off a curb in 2021. The bookshelf leans. Maybe the new place should get a few new things. It's also Friday. Pizza night, the first takeout in nine days.
entries.highlight: Measured all their furniture to prepare for apartment viewings and realized they want to leave some behind.

entries.title: Opening day of the outdoor market
entries.body: The farmers market moved outdoors for the season today, back in the lot behind the library, and it felt like a festival. There was a guy with a banjo instead of the winter fiddle player, and a line for the donut stand that went halfway down the block. I bought asparagus, a bunch of radishes, rhubarb because I'd never cooked it, salad greens, and another loaf of sourdough from the same bakery as in the winter. $41. Ran into Mrs. Okafor from the second floor of my building, who I've only ever spoken to about packages, and we ended up talking for twenty minutes about rhubarb. She told me to make a crumble and to not skimp on the sugar. I told her I'm moving at the end of the summer. She said, good for you. Rhubarb crumble is happening tomorrow.
entries.highlight: Visited the first outdoor farmers market of the season and chatted with a neighbor about rhubarb.

entries.title: Crumble and a disciplined grocery run
entries.body: Went to the grocery store at 8:15 before it got busy, which is now just my Sunday routine. Stuck to the list for once, and for twice, and for, I think, the fifth Sunday in a row. Chicken thighs, rice, eggs, spinach, Greek yogurt, oats, butter, brown sugar for the crumble, and coffee. $64. Then I came home and made Mrs. Okafor's rhubarb crumble. I did not skimp on the sugar. It came out bubbling and pink and so good that I ate a third of it standing at the counter before it had cooled down, and burned my mouth, and kept eating anyway. Took a big square down to the second floor and knocked on Mrs. Okafor's door. She tasted it and said, more sugar next time. Every older woman I know is the same person.
entries.favorite: Burning my mouth on the crumble
entries.highlight: Stuck to the grocery list for the fifth week in a row and baked a rhubarb crumble to share with a neighbor.

entries.title: The apartment with the light
entries.body: Third viewing tonight after work and I think this is it. A second floor one bedroom about fifteen minutes from a different station on the same line, so I can still take the 8:05. It's on a quiet street near the lake. The living room has two huge windows facing west, and at 6:30 tonight the whole room was gold. The kitchen has a window over the sink. The washer and dryer are real, full size, in a closet. The bedroom fits my bed and a dresser and I could still walk around. Rent is $1,890, which is at the top of my range. I stood in the living room in the light for a while and the agent let me. Then I went home and applied, the same night, before I could talk myself out of it.
entries.highlight: Toured a bright second-floor apartment near the lake with in-unit laundry and applied the same night.

entries.title: Approved. Moving September 2nd.
entries.body: The application was approved at 2:14 this afternoon. I was in a meeting about empty states and I saw the email notification and had to sit there and keep talking about blank screens with a straight face while my brain was screaming. Lease starts September 1st. I'm planning to move September 2nd, the day after Labor Day, because movers are cheaper on a Tuesday. I signed it tonight on my laptop, twelve pages, initials on every one. Then I called Mom and she cried a little and then immediately asked if there's room in the yard for a tomato plant. There's no yard, I told her. She said a pot, then. I sat on my old dark couch in my old dark apartment and felt so happy. Took myself out for celebration dumplings. That's a category now.
entries.favorite: Mom asking about a tomato plant
entries.highlight: Got approved for the new apartment, signed the lease, and set September 2nd as moving day.

entries.title: The moving math
entries.body: Monthly budget check-in, which tonight was really the moving math. First month's rent and the security deposit were due at signing, $3,780 total, and I paid it out of the moving fund, which nearly emptied it. I feel faint looking at the balance. But I've been saving since February and the money was there, exactly when I needed it, which is the whole point of saving. Now I need about $1,200 more by September for movers, which got quoted at $850 for a small team for four hours, plus a new dresser and some boxes. That's three months, $400 a month. I moved some money into savings tonight, $300 from this paycheck. Also promised myself to sell the curb dresser instead of moving it. Mrs. Okafor said her nephew might want it.
entries.favorite: The money being there when I needed it
entries.highlight: Paid the new apartment's deposit and first month's rent from the moving fund and planned the remaining savings for movers.

entries.title: Walking the river loop at 6:30
entries.body: Did the long walk before work this morning, the same river loop I did back in March when it was 52 degrees and I thought that was warm. Today it was 68 at 6:30 and already humid. The walk took me 38 minutes instead of 40, which isn't nothing, and the hill back up didn't make me stop once. I used to think walks didn't count as exercise, but on my non-running days they keep me in the habit of getting out the door. The running plan is at week seven now, and the app wants twenty-five minutes with no breaks, which still sounds made up to me. Saturday I made it nineteen before I had to walk. Saw the same old man feeding the ducks that I saw in March. We nodded at each other like colleagues. More awake than usual all morning and I wrote three good design critiques before 10.
entries.highlight: Took a morning walk along the river loop faster than in March and noticed the running plan was building fitness.

entries.title: Free boxes from the liquor store
entries.body: Ran errands after work. First the pharmacy to refill my allergy prescription, which is now a seasonal ritual. Then the liquor store on the corner, which a coworker told me gives away boxes if you ask nicely. I asked nicely. The guy behind the counter, who I've bought exactly two bottles of wine from in three years, gave me eleven sturdy boxes and a roll of packing tape he wasn't using. I carried them home in two trips, looking like a person who's very bad at Tetris. That's eleven boxes I don't have to buy, which is probably about forty dollars. The boxes are now stacked in the hallway, the same hallway that looked huge after the donation runs. It does not look huge now. Pharmacy, boxes, tape, all done by 7. Packing starts this weekend. Twelve weeks until the move.
entries.highlight: Picked up a prescription and got eleven free moving boxes from the local liquor store.

entries.title: Morning yoga, a little less stiff
entries.body: Back to the 6:15 yoga class on Thursday for the first time since February. The woman with the little eye pillow was there again, in the exact same spot by the window. It's like she never left. The difference between this time and January is pretty big. I can touch my toes now, almost, if I bend my knees a little and nobody's looking. The running has made my hips tight in a new way, and the instructor kept doing a pigeon pose that felt like someone untying a knot in my leg. Afterward my head felt clear and quiet all the way to the office. I think yoga is my answer to running shins. Booking it every other Thursday through the summer. Ate lunch outside again. Bench count this month: four.
entries.highlight: Returned to morning yoga for the first time since winter and noticed being more flexible than in January.

entries.title: Helped Sam carry a couch, skipped the run
entries.body: Skipped the Saturday run because I spent the morning helping Sam get a new couch up four flights of stairs. Sam bought it used from a guy online, and it is much bigger than the photos suggested. We had to take the legs off, stand it up on its end, and pivot it around the landing about nine times while yelling pivot at each other like that one TV show. My arms are shaking. Sam bought me lunch as payment, a giant burrito, which I believe is the official currency of moving help. That counts as a workout as far as I'm concerned. I was asleep by 9. My back has asked me to never move a couch again, which is unfortunate, because I'm moving in eleven weeks. Sam has promised to return the favor.
entries.highlight: Helped friend Sam carry a used couch up four flights of stairs instead of running, then went to bed early.

entries.title: Father's Day burgers and the knee
entries.body: Took the morning train to my parents' for Father's Day. Dad wanted burgers on the grill, which he insisted on doing himself, standing on one leg like a flamingo because his knee was bothering him. Mom and I exchanged a look the whole time. I brought him a new grill thermometer and a book about the history of baseball, and he read the first chapter at the table while his burger got cold. The garden looks amazing. The tomatoes we planted on Mother's Day are already up to my waist, and Mom has staked every single one with a precision I can only describe as surgical. After lunch I finally asked Dad about the physical therapy again. He said, I'm thinking about it. Mom said, he's been thinking about it for a year. Still, he didn't say no.
entries.highlight: Spent Father's Day grilling at their parents' house and gently brought up physical therapy for Dad's knee again.

entries.title: Evening yoga after a long Monday
entries.body: Did the 6pm yoga class after work, which I normally avoid because evening plans always lose to work. But my calves were so tight from Saturday's couch carrying that I needed it more than I needed anything else. The evening class is a totally different crowd from the morning one: more people, more chatting, one guy who kept his headphones in the whole time. The instructor did a lot of slow hip openers and one balance pose where I fell over sideways into my mat neighbor, who was very gracious about it. Still, I held the warrior poses longer than I expected. My hamstrings feel like rubber bands that someone finally stopped pulling. I also noticed my brain was quiet during the last ten minutes, which almost never happens on a Monday.
entries.favorite: My quiet brain at the end
entries.highlight: Went to an evening yoga class after a long Monday to stretch out sore legs and felt calmer.

entries.title: Feedback for the second designer hire
entries.body: We're hiring another mid-level designer, and I'm on the interview panel for the first time, which Dana asked me to do as part of the ownership thing. So this morning I blocked two hours for interview feedback and actually kept it. Turned off Slack, put on noise-canceling headphones, and wrote up all three candidates from last week. Last December I wrote feedback like a cooking show judge. This time I tried to write what each person would actually need to succeed here, not just whether I liked them. One of them, a guy named Tomas, did a portfolio presentation that made me rethink how we do our own case studies. I recommended him. Finished by 11:40 and ate lunch in the kitchen with Chloe and Ravi. Good day.
entries.highlight: Sat on an interview panel for the first time and wrote more thoughtful candidate feedback than in the past.

entries.title: Two miles without stopping
entries.body: Before all that work stuff, this morning, I ran two miles without stopping. The running plan said twenty-eight minutes of running, and I just did it, a loop around the park and then out along the river. I've never in my life run two miles without walking. Not in high school, not ever. The last ten minutes I was talking out loud to myself like a lunatic, saying come on, come on, and a woman walking her dog said you got it, and I almost cried. My time was slow, about 14 minutes a mile, but I don't care. A 5K is 3.1 miles. That's 1.1 more. Back in November, I couldn't run six minutes around my parents' block in Dad's windbreaker. I texted Ravi and he sent back about eight exclamation points. I floated through the rest of the day.
entries.favorite: The woman saying you got it
