entries.highlight: Ran two miles without stopping for the first time ever, a big step toward the 5K goal.

entries.title: Spin on tired legs
entries.body: Probably shouldn't have done spin the day after my two mile run, but I'd booked the 6:30am class two weeks ago, and I'm trying to be the kind of person who shows up to the thing they booked. It was rough. Tamsin was in a mood and played nothing but techno, and every time she yelled climb I felt my legs file a formal complaint. I was slow, but I was there. I kept the resistance lower than usual and didn't try to keep up with the guy in the front row, who I'm pretty sure is a professional cyclist or just a very intense dentist. The good news is I didn't die and I made the 8:05. The bad news is my legs are so done that I'm taking the elevator at the office for the rest of the week.
entries.highlight: Took a morning spin class on tired legs the day after a big run and kept the resistance low.

entries.title: Mom's first ripe tomato
entries.body: Called Mom on the walk home and told her about the two miles. She made me tell the whole story twice, once for her and once for Dad, who she put on speaker. Dad said, that's farther than I've walked all year, which was meant as a joke but kind of wasn't. Then Mom announced, very seriously, that the first tomato is ripe. One single cherry tomato, which she split in half with Dad at the kitchen table like it was a ceremony. Her zinnias are blooming and the garden is doing well. She asked about the move, and I told her about the eleven boxes, and she said she'll send me her packing tips, which I know will be a handwritten list mailed in an envelope. I did two extra loops of my block to finish the call.
entries.highlight: Shared news of their two-mile run with their parents and heard about Mom's first ripe tomato.

entries.title: Holiday bathroom deep clean
entries.body: Day off for the holiday. Spent the morning cleaning the bathroom, really cleaning it, the way you do when you're about to get your security deposit judged. Scrubbed the grout with an old toothbrush, descaled the showerhead in a bag of vinegar tied on with a rubber band, which is a trick from Mom's handwritten list that arrived yesterday. Number four on her list says clean as you pack, not after, and she underlined it twice. The tub came out two shades whiter. I also took out the recycling, which was mostly boxes I've already broken down from other people's deliveries. The bathroom frankly looks better than when I moved in. Gus would be proud. Then I packed one box of books, labeled it, and took a break on the fire escape.
entries.highlight: Used a holiday to deep clean the bathroom using Mom's handwritten moving tips and packed the first box.

entries.title: Weights at the gym with a printed plan
entries.body: Went to the gym in the late afternoon since I had the day off. I did weights, which I've been avoiding because the weight room is mostly large men grunting, and I never know what to do in there. Ravi wrote me a simple plan on a sticky note: goblet squats, rows, lunges, push-ups on a bench, three sets of ten each. I printed it out bigger and taped it to my water bottle, which is very cool and not dorky at all. Nobody looked at me once. Turns out everyone in the weight room is too busy looking at themselves in the mirror. I finished every set, which surprised me more than anyone. My arms are still a little sore from Sam's couch. I'm going to do this plan once a week. Ravi says it'll help my running.
entries.highlight: Tried a simple weightlifting routine written by coworker Ravi and felt surprisingly strong.

entries.title: Dana asked me to mentor Chloe
entries.body: Had my 1:1 with Dana this afternoon. I expected to talk about the empty states rollout, but instead she asked if I'd be willing to mentor Chloe officially. A weekly half hour, plus being the person Chloe can ask the questions she doesn't want to ask in meetings. Dana said Chloe asked for me by name, which frankly shocked me. I said yes before Dana even finished the sentence. Then I set up the first one right away, today at 4, coffee in the kitchen. Chloe brought her paper notebook and a list of questions. Her first one was how do I know when a design is done, and I didn't have a good answer, and I told her that, and we talked about it for forty minutes. Left right at 5:30. I'm going to be thinking about her question all weekend.
entries.favorite: Chloe asking for me by name
entries.highlight: Was asked by Dana to officially mentor junior designer Chloe and held their first mentoring session.

entries.title: Change of address, scheduled early
entries.body: Ran errands after work tonight. Post office first, where the line was its usual length, which is to say, long. While I waited, I filled out the mail forwarding form on my phone and scheduled it to start September 2nd. Then the pharmacy for sunscreen, because the beach trip is next week, and a little travel bag of everything. Then the library to return the four books I checked out in April and never opened. I paid a dollar sixty in late fees and the librarian said, it happens, in a voice that told me it happens to me specifically. Three stops, home by 7:40. I'm getting oddly good at errands. I have a route now, a whole efficient loop, like a mail carrier. Two months until the move. Seven boxes packed.
entries.highlight: Ran an evening errand loop, scheduled mail forwarding for the move, and bought sunscreen for the beach trip.

entries.title: Fireworks from Alex's roof
entries.body: Fourth of July. Alex has roof access in their building, which basically makes Alex the most popular person we know for one night a year. Sam and I got there at 7 with chips, a watermelon, and a little portable grill Sam borrowed from a coworker. We grilled corn and hot dogs and Alex's partner Robin made a pitcher of something pink that we were told not to ask about. There were maybe fifteen people up there by sunset, and when the fireworks started over the lake everyone went quiet. I sat on a cooler and watched for twenty minutes without once checking my phone. Sam and I talked about how in two months, I'll be able to see these from near my new place, since it's closer to the lake. Got home at midnight, smelling like charcoal. Very good night.
entries.favorite: Everyone going quiet for the fireworks
entries.highlight: Celebrated the Fourth of July watching fireworks from friend Alex's rooftop with Sam and others.

entries.title: June was a celebration month
entries.body: Budget check-in this morning with leftover watermelon. I'll be honest, June was not great for the eating out line. $310. In my defense, June had a lot of celebrating: the apartment, Alex's promotion, Sam's couch burrito, and the celebration dumplings, which I keep inventing excuses for. Groceries were fine at $244. The main thing is the moving fund, which is back up to $1,120 after the deposit wiped it out last month. I moved some money into savings again, $250, so I'm on track for the movers. The new rule I'm trying: celebrations are allowed, but I have to name what I'm celebrating before I order. If I can't name it in one sentence, it's just takeout. I've also set a beach trip budget of $500 for the week, including my share of the cottage.
entries.highlight: Reviewed a high-spending June, kept the moving fund on track, and set a rule for celebration spending.

entries.title: Pre-vacation errand blitz
entries.body: Afternoon errand blitz before the beach trip. Pharmacy to refill my prescription early, since I'll be gone, plus a new pair of cheap sunglasses because mine snapped at Alex's last night when I sat on them. The pharmacist and I are basically friends now. Then the hardware store for a timer for the lamp, so the apartment looks lived in while I'm away, which feels very Mom of me. Then the laundromat, one last time before vacation, so I have clean everything for the week. I read half a beach novel while the dryer spun, which I guess means I've already started vacation. Four stops in under three hours, which might be a record. Got home, packed a bag, and put it by the door. I'm leaving Tuesday morning. Sam is driving. I'm in charge of snacks and the playlist.
entries.favorite: Starting the beach novel at the laundromat
entries.highlight: Ran pre-vacation errands, including a prescription refill and laundry, and packed for a beach trip with friends.

entries.title: Canceled the meal kit I outgrew
entries.body: Paid rent and the utility bills before the trip. Rent is $1,650 for two more months, and then it's goodbye forever. While doing bills I canceled the meal kit subscription I started in March. It was useful when I didn't know how to cook anything, because it came with the instructions and the exact amount of every ingredient. But now I mostly cook from Mom's recipes and the internet, and I've been skipping the boxes half the time. It was costing me $60 a week when I didn't skip. That's a weird, nice feeling, outgrowing a thing that was supposed to teach you how to do something. Like training wheels. I'm putting the money toward a decent chef's knife instead, which I've been wanting since the cast iron. Then I packed my beach bag again, for the third time.
entries.highlight: Paid bills and canceled a meal kit subscription after learning to cook without it.

entries.title: Beach day one: notifications off
entries.body: First day of a week at the beach. Sam, Alex, Robin, and I split a little gray cottage two blocks from the ocean, $380 each for the week, with a porch that sags in the middle and an outdoor shower that is the best thing I've ever experienced. We got here at 1. Before I even unpacked, I did something I've never done on vacation: I turned off work notifications. Not just muted, actually logged out of Slack and email on my phone. I set an out of office that says I'm back on the 15th and Marcus has the empty states questions. Then I lay on a towel and read a whole book, start to finish, a mystery Sam lent me. I didn't check my phone once. The waves were loud and the sand was hot and I felt my shoulders drop for the first time in about a year.
entries.highlight: Started a week-long beach vacation with friends, turned off work notifications completely, and read a whole book.

entries.title: Spare key to Mrs. Okafor at 7am
entries.body: This morning before Sam picked me up, I did the last-minute leaving-town stuff. Watered the plant and moved it away from the window so it wouldn't fry. Set the lamp timer for 8pm to 11pm. Took out the trash, which I learned from the fridge purge last Thanksgiving is very important. Then I knocked on Mrs. Okafor's door at 7am, which felt rude, but she was already up with her coffee and in a housecoat, and I gave her my spare key in case anything happens. She told me to bring her back a shell. Then she asked if I wanted a muffin for the road, and I said no, and she gave me two. Sam pulled up at 7:20 honking the horn. I had the snacks and the playlist ready. We stopped for gas and iced coffee and were on the highway by 7:45.
entries.highlight: Took care of last-minute tasks before the beach trip and left a spare key with neighbor Mrs. Okafor.

entries.title: Running on the beach at sunrise
entries.body: Day four of the beach, which is technically a Friday, which I keep forgetting because I've stopped knowing what day it is. I got up at 5:45 and went for a run on the beach at sunrise, on the hard sand near the water. It's much harder than running in the park. My feet sink with every step and my calves were screaming after ten minutes. I did a mile and a half, walked back, and then just stood in the cold water up to my knees while the sun came up pink. There was a guy with a metal detector who said good morning, and two pelicans flew by in formation like they were in an air show. Got back to the cottage and Sam was making French toast on the old stove. We ate on the saggy porch. This is the first vacation where I haven't thought about work once. Not once.
entries.highlight: Ran on the beach at sunrise during vacation and realized they had not thought about work all trip.

entries.title: Six hundred emails and a late train
entries.body: First full week back from the beach and I'm still sunburned on the tops of my feet. The 8:05 showed up at 8:22. I cleared my inbox on the platform, which takes longer when you come back to six hundred emails. Actually, I came back on Tuesday to six hundred and fourteen, and as of this morning I'm down to thirty. Most of them were automated, to be fair. Got in just in time for the design review, where Chloe presented her first big piece of work, the new account settings layout. She was nervous but she was great, and when Elena asked a tough question about edge cases, Chloe answered it calmly, using an approach we talked about in our mentoring session. I didn't say anything. I just sat there trying not to look proud. I was proud. Marcus did handle everything while I was out, too.
entries.highlight: Caught up on email after vacation and watched mentee Chloe present her first major design confidently.

entries.title: Alex talks about Robin, seriously
entries.body: Got coffee with Alex at 7:15 before the train, like our December walks. Alex got an iced oat latte and I got regular iced coffee, which I'm now willing to pay four dollars for because it's 82 degrees at 7am. We walked around the block twice. Alex was quiet for a while and then said, I think Robin is it for me. Not in a dramatic way, just very sure. They've been together almost four years. Alex hasn't asked yet and isn't planning to anytime soon, but wanted to say it out loud to someone. I said that I've seen how Alex is around Robin, and I'm not surprised at all. We both got a little teary in front of a bodega, which was a little embarrassing. I made the 8:05 with one minute to spare. What a nice way to start a Monday.
entries.highlight: Had early coffee with Alex, who shared that their partner Robin feels like the one.

entries.title: Laps at the public pool
entries.body: Went for a swim after work at the outdoor public pool by the park. It's open until 8 in the summer and costs four dollars. I haven't swum laps since high school, and it shows. I did twenty laps, which sounds like a lot, until you realize that I stopped at the wall after each one to breathe like a wheezing accordion. A lifeguard who looked about sixteen kept watching me, maybe concerned. But it felt amazing to be cool on a 90 degree day, and it didn't hurt my shins at all, which running does sometimes. My shoulders were burning by lap twelve, and one calf cramped in the deep end, which was exciting for everyone. Afterward I sat on the edge of the pool and watched the sun go down behind the trees. The water smelled like chlorine and summer. I want to come back every Wednesday until it closes.
entries.favorite: Sitting on the edge at sunset
entries.highlight: Swam twenty laps at the outdoor public pool after work for the first time since high school.

entries.title: Packing books, counting books
entries.body: Worked from home today, so in the morning before standup I packed the bookshelf. I own a hundred and forty-three books. I know that because I counted them, which was a mistake, because now I know. I put twenty in a donation pile, mostly ones I bought and never read, plus the cookbook I got in 2020 and only opened to put a coffee mug on. That one I kept, actually, because I might use it now. Funny how that works. Vacuumed behind the bookshelf, where I found what was either a lot of dust or a small animal. It was dust. Took out the recycling. The living room looks emptier now, which is strange. Five weeks until the move. Twelve boxes packed. The liquor store boxes are holding up.
entries.highlight: Packed and counted their 143 books before work, donating twenty, five weeks before the move.

entries.title: Stir-fry with the new knife
entries.body: The chef's knife came, the one I bought with the meal kit money, and I made a stir-fry tonight just to use it. I cannot stress enough how different chopping is with a sharp knife. My old knife was basically a butter knife with ambition. I sliced an onion thin enough to see through, and I cut a bell pepper in about eight seconds. The stir-fry had chicken, snap peas, bell pepper, scallions, garlic, ginger, and the sauce I've been making since April with soy sauce, honey, and rice vinegar, plus some chili crisp now. Listened to a podcast about how knives are made, which was maybe too on theme. Dinner was great, and I didn't cut myself, which was my main goal. I put the knife on the counter and admired it like a trophy.
entries.highlight: Made a stir-fry using a new chef's knife bought with money saved by canceling a meal kit.

entries.title: Mom has too many tomatoes
entries.body: Called Mom on the walk home. She has hit the part of summer she calls the tomato emergency, where there are so many ripe tomatoes that she's giving them to neighbors who are now avoiding her. She's made eleven jars of sauce. She asked if I wanted some and I said yes, absolutely, mail me sauce, and she said she'd bring it when they come to see the new place. That's the first time she's mentioned visiting the new apartment, which made me realize, oh, they'll come here. I'll have a real place for them to visit, with light and a kitchen window. Dad says hi. His knee was bad this week because of the heat and humidity, Mom says. She also says he's been walking to the mailbox and back every evening, like his own physical therapy. That's something.
entries.highlight: Heard about Mom's overflowing tomato harvest and her plan to visit the new apartment.

entries.title: Early walk to beat the heat
entries.body: It's been too hot to run in the mornings this week, 79 degrees at 6am, so I did a long walk instead. I went at 5:50, which is the earliest I've been outside on purpose in years. The river loop looks different at that hour. Lots of runners, a few people walking dogs, and the bakery on the corner had its back door open so the whole block smelled like bread. I've been thinking about my running plan. I finished the official nine weeks right before vacation, but I've only run three times since, partly because of the heat, and partly because packing has taken over my evenings and weekends. I don't want to lose the two miles. But I also don't want to beat myself up about it. So walks count. I was at my desk by 8:30 with a clear head and bread on my mind.
entries.highlight: Took an early walk to beat the heat while reflecting on a dip in running during the busy pre-move weeks.

entries.title: The curb dresser finds a home
entries.body: Mrs. Okafor's nephew came by this morning to pick up the dresser I found on the curb in 2021. He's a college kid who just got his first apartment, and he looked at it like it was a treasure. I sold it to him for forty dollars, which is exactly forty dollars more than I paid for it. We carried it down three flights together and it took about fifteen minutes and several new swear words. Then I changed the sheets and took out the recycling, and ordered a new dresser for the new apartment, a simple one with drawers that actually slide, $310, scheduled to arrive September 3rd. One less thing to carry down three flights in September. It felt nice to know that my old curb dresser is starting a new chapter. Me too, sort of. Four weeks.
entries.highlight: Sold their old curb-found dresser to a neighbor's nephew and ordered a new one for the new apartment.

entries.title: Setting up utilities at the new place
entries.body: Paid rent and the bills tonight, and then did all the boring adult setup for the new apartment. Opened an electric account for the new address starting September 1st and set up autopay on day one, which past me would never believe. Scheduled internet installation for September 3rd between 8am and noon, which means I'll have to work from home that morning. I'll be calling the old electric company to close my account on the 2nd. I also canceled a subscription I never use, a fitness app I downloaded in January and haven't opened since February. $9.99 a month, gone. The moving fund is at $1,680, which covers the movers with room for boxes and a few groceries for the first week. I made a moving day checklist in the spreadsheet, with forty-two items. Number one is don't panic.
entries.highlight: Set up utilities and internet for the new apartment and confirmed the moving fund covers the movers.

entries.title: Ravi's numbers on empty states
entries.body: Had a 1:1 with Ravi about the roadmap doc, because he's been pulling the numbers on the empty states project. Phase one went live in June. New users who see the redesigned empty screens are completing their first setup step eleven percent more often than before. Eleven percent. That's real. Ravi showed me a chart and a lot of math I didn't fully understand and he was very excited about the confidence interval. We figured out a plan in twenty minutes for how to present it at the all-hands next week, which Dana arranged. Ravi said, you know this is your project, right? You should present it. I said maybe we both do. Ate lunch at my desk again, which I'll admit is happening more since vacation, because there's so much to catch up on. Need to fix that.
entries.highlight: Reviewed data with coworker Ravi showing the empty states project improved new-user setup by eleven percent.

entries.title: Interview feedback and a packed train
entries.body: Stayed late to finish interview feedback before the hiring committee meets tomorrow. We're hiring again, a senior designer this time, and there were four candidates this week. I ordered pad thai to my desk and finished at 7:45. The feedback took longer than it should have because I tried to write it the way I learned in June, focusing on what each person would need here, and it's slower but better. Tomas, the designer we hired in June, sat in on two interviews with me and asked better questions than I did. The train home was packed with people coming from a baseball game, everyone wearing the same jersey and singing, and I stood squished between two very happy guys for twenty minutes. Got home at 8:40 and didn't do any packing. Tomorrow.
entries.highlight: Worked late to finish thoughtful interview feedback for a senior designer hire and rode home on a crowded train.

entries.title: Closet packed before the train
entries.body: Before work this morning, I packed the closet, because I knew tonight would be a late one. I'm trying out Mom's tip number seven: pack clothes on their hangers in garbage bags, so you can just hang them back up. It works, and it's very satisfying, like moving a closet in one piece. I also found three things I'd forgotten I owned, including a suit jacket I wore once to a wedding and a hat shaped like a lobster from a work party. The lobster hat stays. I'm not explaining that. Took out the recycling, which at this point is ninety percent the cardboard from my own boxes collapsing. I left at 7:40 for the 8:05. Three weeks until the move, and the apartment is starting to echo. Seventeen boxes packed.
entries.highlight: Packed the closet before work using Mom's hanger trick and found forgotten items, including a lobster-shaped hat.

entries.title: Eating down the pantry
entries.body: Went to the grocery store at 8, my usual time, but kept it small on purpose, because I'm trying to eat down the pantry before the move. I don't want to carry a bag of lentils and four cans of chickpeas across the city. So the list was short: tofu, onions, eggs, apples, a bag of spinach, and coffee. $29. The cheapest grocery trip of the year. The rest of this week's dinners are going to be pantry experiments, like pasta with chickpeas and the last of Mom's tomato sauce, or rice and lentils with whatever spices are left. Last year my pantry was mostly ramen and a bag of rice. Now it has three kinds of vinegar. I don't know when I turned into someone with three kinds of vinegar, but I'm taking two of them with me.
entries.highlight: Kept the grocery run small to use up pantry food before the move, spending only $29.

entries.title: Thirty laps, fewer stops
entries.body: Went to the public pool in the afternoon for my Saturday swim. It was packed with kids and a summer camp group doing cannonballs, but the lap lanes were mostly empty. Did thirty laps today. Three weeks ago I stopped at the wall after every single one. Today I stopped every three. That's the kind of improvement I can see, which I really need right now, because running has been on and off for a while. My shoulders are getting a little stronger and I've figured out how to breathe on both sides, sort of. My arms felt like cooked noodles on the walk home. The lifeguard from before was there again and I swear he looked relieved. Afterward I lay on a towel on the warm concrete and fell asleep for twenty minutes. The pool closes Labor Day. I'll miss this.
entries.highlight: Swam thirty laps at the public pool with far fewer breaks than three weeks earlier.

entries.title: My name on the all-hands slide
entries.body: All-hands this morning, and it ran long, as always. But this time, slide fourteen was empty states, and at the top it said design lead and my name. Dana introduced it and then handed it to me and Ravi. I talked for four minutes. Four minutes. I'd practiced it on the train twice, quietly, like a crazy person. I showed the grid of thirty-one blank screens from February, and then the new versions, and then Ravi showed the eleven percent. People clapped. The CEO said great work by name. I thought about January, sitting in that same room, clapping for my own work with someone else's name on it. Then back-to-back calls until lunch and nothing else done until 3. Marcus sent me a message that just said, slide fourteen. That's all. I knew what he meant.
entries.highlight: Presented the empty states project at the all-hands with their name on the slide, a contrast to feeling unseen in January.

entries.title: Last prescription at the old pharmacy
entries.body: Ran errands after work, still floating from the all-hands. Went to the pharmacy and refilled my prescription and transferred it to the pharmacy near the new apartment, which is the kind of thing I would have forgotten until I ran out in October. The pharmacist who I've been seeing for three years said, oh, you're leaving us, and I felt weirdly sad about it. She told me the new pharmacy is good but slow. Then the post office to buy a few stamps, and to confirm the forwarding was set, because I don't trust the website. The line was short for once. Then the hardware store, for more packing tape and a box cutter. Three stops, and every one of them was a small goodbye. Two weeks. Twenty-two boxes. The apartment has started to sound like a gym when I talk.
entries.favorite: The pharmacist saying you're leaving us
entries.highlight: Transferred their prescription to a pharmacy near the new apartment and confirmed mail forwarding.

entries.title: Wrapping the kitchen in newspaper
entries.body: Packed the kitchen this morning before work. All the dishes wrapped in newspaper, which Mrs. Okafor gave me a stack of, because apparently she still gets the paper and saves it for exactly this kind of situation. Kept out one plate, one bowl, one mug, one fork, and the cast iron, because I'm not living on takeout for two weeks. I'm too far along for that now. The cast iron goes in last, in its own box, labeled fragile in capital letters even though it's literally indestructible. I just love it. Also changed the sheets, since I'm not sure when I'll be able to find them in the new place. My kitchen now echoes when I set down a mug. Then I went to work with newspaper ink all over my hands, which Chloe noticed immediately and asked if I'd been doing calligraphy.
entries.highlight: Packed the kitchen before work, keeping out only the basics and the cast iron pan.

entries.title: Sam is quietly miserable at work
entries.body: Got coffee with Sam this morning near the park, and we walked around the block twice, and then once more, because Sam had a lot to say. Sam's job is wearing them down. A new boss, a lot of reorganizing, and the kind of meetings where nobody decides anything. Sam's been there five years and says it feels like being stuck in the same room with the lights getting slowly dimmer. I mostly listened. I told Sam about how Alex practiced asking for the promotion, and about my empty states pitch, and how both things started with saying the thing out loud. Sam said, yeah, but I don't even know what I'd ask for. That's fair. Then we confirmed the moving day plan: Sam and Alex arrive at 8am on the 2nd, pizza is on me. Made plans to do coffee again soon.
entries.highlight: Had coffee with Sam, who is unhappy at work, and confirmed friends' help for moving day.

entries.title: Saturday haircut, new neighborhood ready
entries.body: Nico has Saturday hours, so I went in for a haircut this afternoon instead of my usual lunch break. Kept it short, since it's still hot and I'm about to sweat through moving day. Nico asked what's new and I told him about the move, the new place, the light, the kitchen window, and he said, you seem different than in February. I asked how, and he said, you talk faster when you're excited now. In February you talked slow. I don't know what that means, but I think he meant it as a compliment. $40 this time because I tipped extra. It's a fifteen minute train ride from the new place to his shop, and I already decided I'll keep coming. New haircut, almost new zip code.
entries.favorite: Nico saying I talk faster when excited
entries.highlight: Got a Saturday haircut before the move, and the barber noticed they seemed more excited and energized.

entries.title: Phase two deck, with Chloe on screens
entries.body: Blocked off the morning for the empty states phase two deck and actually kept it, which is harder than it used to be because more people need me now. That's a good problem, I know. Turned off Slack for two hours. The new thing is that I asked Chloe to design four of the screens for phase two herself, instead of me doing all of them and her watching. Dana's ownership advice, but passed down a level. Chloe's screens came in this morning and two of them are better than what I would have done. One is a little too clever, with an animation that I think would get annoying the fifth time you saw it. I'll tell her that at our Wednesday mentoring session, carefully. Got a full draft done before lunch. Ate lunch outside with Ravi. One week until the move.
entries.favorite: Chloe's screens being better than mine
entries.highlight: Finished the phase two deck during focus time and had mentee Chloe design several of the screens herself.

entries.title: Last Friday in the dark apartment
entries.body: Skipped the workout and went to bed at 9:30. I'm writing this from a mattress on the floor, because the bed frame is already taken apart and leaning against the wall. This whole week has been packing every night after work. Twenty-nine boxes now, plus the hanger bags, plus a lamp I'm wrapping in a towel like a baby. My lower back has opinions about all of this, and it's sharing them. I lay here for a while looking at the ceiling, at the water stain shaped like a rabbit I've stared at for three years. I'm going to miss the rabbit, a little. Not the radiator. Not the laundromat. But this was the apartment where I learned to cook, and where I wrote the index card. Four more days. I'm so tired. Good tired.
entries.highlight: Skipped a workout after a week of packing and reflected on their last days in the old apartment.

entries.title: August budget: the moving month
entries.body: Budget check-in for August. Eating out was $280, which is high, and I knew it would be, because once the kitchen got packed I lived on the dumpling place and sandwiches. I'm calling it a moving exception and not beating myself up. Groceries were only $163, because of the pantry clean-out. The moving fund is at $1,840, which covers the movers at $850, plus a tip, plus the new dresser that's already paid for. There'll be a little left over, maybe $600, and I've already decided that's the start of an emergency fund. Here's what got me: I looked back at the spreadsheet from last November, when the takeout number was $412 and I had zero dollars saved. Ten months. That's the whole difference. Moving in two days. Signed off the old electric account tonight.
entries.highlight: Reviewed August's moving-month budget, confirmed the moving fund covers costs, and planned to start an emergency fund.

entries.title: Labor Day spin, then the last boxes
entries.body: Labor Day. No work. I went to the 8am spin class at my old gym one last time, since I've already signed up for a new gym near the new place that has an indoor pool. Tamsin was teaching, of course. When I told her it was my last class she made the entire room do one extra climb in my honor, which nobody thanked me for. I was slow and a little sentimental, and it was a good goodbye. Then I came home and packed the last six boxes, taped them up, and took apart the bookshelf, which fell apart in my hands like it had been waiting for permission. Ordered the last dumplings from the dumpling place for dinner and ate them on the floor. The guy at the counter said see you next week, and I didn't have the heart to tell him.
entries.favorite: Tamsin's extra climb in my honor
entries.highlight: Took a final spin class at their old gym on Labor Day and finished packing the night before the move.

entries.title: Moving day: pizza on the floor
entries.body: Moving day. The movers came at 8 for the furniture, and Sam and Alex showed up at 8:05 with coffees and took on the boxes. Thirty-five boxes down three flights. Sam kept saying pivot every time we turned a corner, as revenge for the couch. Mrs. Okafor came out in her housecoat to wave goodbye and gave me a plant cutting in a jam jar. The new place is so much bright. Brighter. I'm too tired for grammar. By 2pm everything was in, and the movers were gone, $850 plus a $100 tip. We ate pizza on the floor of the living room in a big square of sunlight, because the couch was covered in boxes. Alex hung a string of lights on the window. Sam opened every cabinet in the kitchen and said you have space. I do. I have space. And light.
entries.highlight: Moved into the new apartment with help from friends Sam and Alex, celebrating with pizza on the sunny living room floor.

entries.title: First bills at the new address
entries.body: Worked from home this morning for the internet installation, which happened at 11:52, eight minutes before the window closed. Very dramatic. Then I paid bills at the new address for the first time. Rent is $1,890, which is $240 more than the old place. But I did the math tonight: I'm not paying $32 a month at the laundromat anymore, and the electric should be lower because the windows actually close. So the real difference is closer to $180. I set up autopay for the electric bill, which I did in advance, and put the new rent amount into the spreadsheet. There's a little hollow feeling when you see the bigger number, but then I look up and the whole living room is lit up at 4pm. I'm paying for light. I knew that going in. It's worth it.
entries.highlight: Paid the first bills at the new apartment and calculated that the true rent increase is smaller than it looks.

entries.title: Met Priya across the hall
entries.body: After work tonight I was dragging a giant stack of flattened boxes down to the recycling, and the woman across the hall came out and grabbed half of the stack without even asking. Her name is Priya. She's a nurse at the hospital by the lake and works three night shifts a week, so she said if I ever hear her coming in at 7am, that's why. She's lived here four years and gave me a full building briefing on the walk down: the package room is in the basement, the recycling guy comes Thursday, and the radiator in my unit is good, which is a sentence nobody has ever said to me. She has a balcony full of herbs and said I can take basil whenever I want. I donated the two bags of stuff that didn't fit on the way back. A good neighbor already.
entries.favorite: Priya saying my radiator is good
entries.highlight: Met neighbor Priya, a nurse across the hall, while recycling moving boxes, and she offered basil from her balcony garden.

entries.title: Learning the new errand route
entries.body: Ran errands after work to learn the new neighborhood. The new pharmacy is, as my old pharmacist warned me, good but slow. I waited twenty-five minutes for my refill while a man ahead of me argued about the price of foot cream. The post office here is tiny and has a cat, a real one, sitting on the counter. The line was long, which seems to be a universal post office law, but the cat made it bearable. Then the hardware store two blocks over, which has a guy named Walt who helped me find the right curtain rods for the big windows and also told me which bagel place is the good one, unprompted. I now know where to buy stamps, curtain rods, and a bagel within six blocks, which feels like citizenship. It's going to take a while to build a new route. I already like the cat.
entries.highlight: Explored the new neighborhood's pharmacy, post office, and hardware store while running errands.

entries.title: First swim at the new gym
entries.body: Went to the new gym after errands, for my first swim in the indoor pool. The new gym is six minutes from my apartment, which is about twenty minutes closer than the old one, so I'm out of excuses. The pool is a little warmer than the public pool was, with four lanes and a big clock on the wall. I did thirty-two laps and stopped every four. That's better than August. My shoulders felt strong today, and I guess the pool kept the swimming from the summer alive. The locker room smells like eucalyptus, which is a big step up from the old gym's smell, which was mostly socks. My legs were already heavy from carrying boxes up and down the stairs all week, so I kept the kick easy. I'm planning on swimming Wednesday and Friday, and running on weekends by the lake.
entries.highlight: Swam thirty-two laps at the new gym's indoor pool, just six minutes from the new apartment.

entries.title: Laundry at 10pm, in my own home
entries.body: Spent the morning vacuuming before work, which is a lot easier when your apartment isn't full of boxes. I'm down to four boxes left to unpack, all labeled misc, which means I'm afraid of them. Also took out the recycling, which here is a little room in the basement with a sign that says please break down your boxes in three languages. But here's the real news. Last night at 10pm, I did a load of laundry. In my apartment. In my pajamas. I didn't walk three blocks with a giant blue bag, I didn't wait for a dryer to open up, I didn't read a book on a plastic chair. I just put the clothes in, and then I went to bed. I know it's small. But I stood there listening to the dryer like it was music. In-unit laundry is the best investment I've ever made.
entries.highlight: Vacuumed the new apartment and celebrated doing laundry at home for the first time with in-unit machines.

entries.title: 6:15 swim, lake fog outside
entries.body: Did a swim before work at 6:15. When I walked to the gym it was foggy and the lake was completely invisible, just a white wall at the end of the street. The pool was nearly empty. Just me and an older woman in a flowered swim cap who swam about three times as fast as me without seeming to try. I was slow, but I swam thirty laps. The new thing is that the train station is close to the gym, so I can swim, shower, and still make the 8:05, which is the first time my workout and my commute have worked together. Last night I slept better knowing I had the swim planned. I'm noticing that my routines are coming back faster than I thought they would after the move. That flowered swim cap is my new goal.
entries.favorite: The woman in the flowered swim cap
entries.highlight: Swam before work on a foggy morning and found the new gym and train station work well together.

entries.title: New store, new aisles, no garlic
entries.body: First real weekly grocery run in the new neighborhood. The store here is bigger than my old one and I spent fifteen minutes just wandering, because I didn't know where anything was. They have a whole aisle of hot sauce. A whole aisle. Got salmon, oat milk, apples, chicken thighs, rice, broccoli, yogurt, and a bag of the good coffee. $91, which is high, but I was stocking the new pantry from almost nothing. Then I got home and realized I forgot garlic, the one thing I went for, because I need it for the pesto I'm making with Priya's basil. Classic. Except this time I just walked to the corner store two blocks away, which here is open late and has garlic, and was back in nine minutes. A forgotten item is a lot less tragic when the store is close.
entries.favorite: The whole aisle of hot sauce
entries.highlight: Did the first big grocery run in the new neighborhood, forgot garlic, but easily got it at the corner store.

entries.title: Dana mentions onboarding, next year
entries.body: Had a 1:1 with Dana this afternoon about the phase two slide deck. We figured out a plan in twenty minutes: launch it in October, measure in November, write it up in December. Then she leaned back and said something interesting. Next year, the company wants to completely redesign onboarding, the first week a new user spends in the product. It's going to be big, it's going to be messy, and it's going to need someone who's done this kind of thing before. She didn't say me. She didn't say not me. She said, keep that in your head. I've been keeping it in my head all evening. A year ago I would have just waited to see if someone picked me. Now I'm thinking about what I'd need to show to be the obvious choice. Got some useful feedback on the deck too.
entries.favorite: Dana saying keep that in your head
entries.highlight: Planned the phase two rollout with Dana, who hinted at a big onboarding redesign next year.

entries.title: WFH with laundry and the bakery
entries.body: Worked from home today, from the little desk I set up by the west window. It's still a little weird to work in a room this bright. I did two loads of laundry between calls, starting the wash at 9:30 and switching it to the dryer after standup, which is a kind of productivity I never had before. The big win, though, was lunch. I took a real lunch break, an actual hour, and walked to the bakery by the lake that Walt from the hardware store recommended. I got a spinach and feta pastry and sat on a bench looking at the water for twenty minutes. Not at my desk. Not at a screen. Then I got back and fixed two design bugs that had been bothering me for weeks, because my brain had space. Left right at 5:30.
entries.favorite: The spinach and feta pastry by the lake
entries.highlight: Worked from home, did laundry between calls, and took a real lunch break by the lake.

entries.title: The lake path, one rusty mile
entries.body: Sunday morning, I walked the lake path for the first time. It's a paved trail that runs along the water for miles, and at 8am it's full of runners, cyclists, and people with strollers. I planned to just walk, but about ten minutes in I started running, for no reason, just because everyone else was. I lasted one mile before I had to stop. One. In June I ran two without stopping. The move and the packing ate my running habit, and I can feel it, in my lungs mostly. So I walked the rest, another forty minutes. The leaves are just starting to turn on the trees near the beach. I'm not going to panic about the mile. I'm going to come back to this path next Sunday and see what happens.
entries.highlight: Walked and ran on the lake path for the first time, noticing their running fitness had slipped during the move.

entries.title: Sunday swim, no stops for six laps
entries.body: Went to the pool Sunday afternoon instead of the lake path, because it rained all morning. The pool on Sunday afternoons is mostly families, so I shared a lane with a dad teaching his daughter to swim with a foam noodle, which made me smile every time I passed them. I did thirty-four laps. Here's the new thing: I did six laps in a row without stopping at the wall. Six. I think it's because I finally figured out how to breathe every three strokes without panicking. A man in the next lane told me, kindly, that I kick from my knees instead of my hips, which explains why my thighs are on fire. Afterward I sat in the hot tub for ten minutes with two retirees who were discussing their cholesterol in detail. Then I napped on the couch for an hour, which was not the plan.
entries.favorite: The dad with the foam noodle
entries.highlight: Swam six laps in a row without stopping for the first time after figuring out their breathing rhythm.

entries.title: Sam's first real job search
entries.body: Got coffee with Sam at the café near my new station before work, which Sam came all the way across town for. That says something. Sam has started looking for a new job, officially, with a spreadsheet and everything. The breaking point was apparently a meeting about a meeting about the reorg. Sam's thinking about leaving the field entirely and maybe moving into something mission-driven, like climate or education. They've updated their resume for the first time in five years and said it felt like reading about a stranger. We walked down to the corner and back after, and Sam said, I'm going to take my time and do it right, even if it takes a year. That sounded very wise to me. I promised to read their cover letters. They promised to come over for dinner once I unpack the last misc boxes.
entries.favorite: Sam coming all the way across town
entries.highlight: Had coffee with Sam, who has officially started a careful job search for more meaningful work.

entries.title: Homemade pesto with Priya's basil
entries.body: Back in January I made pasta with pesto from a jar and said maybe someday I'd make the pesto myself. Tonight I did. Priya left a big bag of basil on my doorknob this morning with a note that just said use it before it dies, which I think is also how she talks to patients. So I blended the basil with garlic, the one I forgot two weeks ago and finally have, toasted pine nuts, parmesan, olive oil, a squeeze of lemon. It was so green it looked fake. Tossed it with pasta and the last of some roasted chicken. It was so much better than the jar that I felt a little betrayed by the jar. I brought a jar of it across the hall to Priya, who tasted it with a spoon right in the doorway and said, okay, you can keep getting basil.
entries.favorite: Priya's note on the basil bag
entries.highlight: Made homemade pesto for the first time using neighbor Priya's basil and shared a jar with her.

entries.title: Wednesday swim, finally a rhythm
entries.body: Swam after work tonight. I've done Wednesday and Friday swims for four weeks straight now, which is the most consistent I've been with anything exercise related since the spring running plan. I think the trick is that the gym is so close. There's no gap between deciding to go and being there, so my brain doesn't have time to argue. Did thirty-six laps, with sets of six. The flowered swim cap woman was there and she nodded at me, which I'm choosing to believe is because she recognizes me as a regular now. My shoulders didn't give out until the last set. It's getting dark at 6:45 now, and I know from last year that I'm going to want to hibernate soon. I'm trying to get ahead of it by keeping the swim days locked in.
entries.highlight: Completed four straight weeks of twice-weekly swims, the most consistent exercise routine since spring.

entries.title: Friday swim skipped, early bed
entries.body: Skipped the Friday swim, which breaks my four week streak. Phase two went live today, and there was a small bug where one of Chloe's screens showed up in the wrong place on tablets, and we were fixing it until 6. It was fine. Nobody panicked. Chloe found the bug herself, which frankly made me proud. But by the time I got home I didn't have anything left. I was in bed by 9:15 and needed it. I'm trying something new, which is not considering a skipped workout as a failure, just as information. The information today is that launch days are not workout days, and that's okay. Slept better than I have all week, and the light in the bedroom this morning was so nice that I just lay there for a while before getting up.
entries.highlight: Skipped a swim on a busy launch day for phase two and chose to treat it as information rather than failure.

entries.title: Mom and Dad are coming Saturday
entries.body: Called Mom on the walk home from the station. The new walk is different, along a street lined with maple trees that are going orange, and only about seven minutes, so I ended up walking an extra loop to keep talking. Mom and Dad are coming to visit Saturday. Their first time seeing the new place. Mom is bringing three jars of tomato sauce and a pot of chives, and she's asking a lot of questions about the light, like she's planning to grow something in my living room. Dad's worried about the stairs. It's only one flight, I told him, with a railing. He said a flight is a flight. His knee has been worse this fall, and he's using a cane on bad days now, which Mom told me quietly. I'm going to clean the whole apartment Friday night.
entries.favorite: Mom planning to grow something in my living room
entries.highlight: Called Mom to plan their parents' first visit to the new apartment and learned Dad's knee has worsened.

entries.title: Mom and Dad see the new place
entries.body: Mom and Dad came on the 10:15 train. We went to the art museum first, because Mom has wanted to see the new textile exhibit for weeks. Dad lasted about an hour and then sat on a bench in front of a big painting of a ship, which he says was the best part. We spent way too long in the gift shop and Mom bought me a print of a botanical drawing for my wall. Then the apartment. Dad did the stairs slowly, with the railing, and said not bad at the top. Mom walked straight to the window, put her hand on the glass, and said, oh, this is good light. She put the chives on the sill. I made them lunch with the cast iron, her own tomato sauce on pasta. Dad said it tastes like home, which is because it literally is.
entries.favorite: Mom saying this is good light
entries.highlight: Hosted their parents for the first time at the new apartment after a trip to the art museum.

entries.title: First full month in the new place
entries.body: First budget check-in for a full month in the new apartment. Rent is up, but laundry is zero, and the electric bill came in at $61, compared to $96 in the old drafty place. So the real difference really is closer to $180, like I hoped. Groceries were $236, even with the pantry restock. Eating out was $152, the lowest month ever. I think it's because the kitchen here is nice enough that I actually want to be in it. I moved some money into savings, $300, into the emergency fund, which is at $940 now. My new goal: three months of expenses, which would be about $10,000. That's far away. But last November I had nothing, and now I have a new apartment, and the beginning of a safety net. I'll get there.
entries.highlight: Reviewed the first full month's budget in the new apartment, found lower utility costs, and set an emergency fund goal.

entries.title: Weights before work, new gym edition
entries.body: Did weights before work, the first time at the new gym's weight room, which is smaller and much calmer than the old one. There's an older man who does very slow curls while listening to opera on a speaker clipped to his belt, which frankly sets a nice tone. I used Ravi's sticky note plan from June, which I still have taped to my water bottle, faded now: goblet squats, rows, lunges, push-ups on a bench. I've lost some strength since summer, I could feel it in the push-ups, but not as much as I feared. Standup felt shorter than usual, which I'm crediting to the squats. I made the 8:05 and spent the train ride planning phase three. I should probably update the sticky note. Maybe I'll ask Ravi for a new one.
entries.highlight: Did a first weightlifting session at the new gym using coworker Ravi's old routine.

entries.title: Friday night meal prep so Sunday is free
entries.body: Tried something new: I meal-prepped on Friday night instead of Sunday, so the weekend could be completely free. Salmon and rice bowls for Monday and Tuesday, since salmon doesn't keep long, plus a big tray of roasted sweet potatoes and chickpeas for the rest of the week. Took about two hours with a podcast on, a long one about a famous art heist, which made me want to go back to the museum. Weekday me will be grateful, and so will weekend me. The kitchen here is so much easier to cook in. There's actual counter space, so I'm not chopping on a cutting board balanced on top of the stove like before. I can lay out all five containers in a row. I took a photo of them lined up like soldiers and sent it to Mom, who replied with a thumbs up and the word finally.
entries.highlight: Meal-prepped a week of lunches on Friday night to free up the weekend, enjoying the new kitchen's counter space.

entries.title: The rent autopay and a goodbye to cable
entries.body: Paid rent and the utility bills this morning. Well, the autopay paid them, and I checked that it worked, which is my new job. I also set up autopay for the rent itself, which the new building allows online, so now basically nothing in my life requires me to remember a due date. Then I finally killed the cable channel package I added two years ago to watch one cooking competition, which I haven't watched since. $22 a month, which is $264 a year for a channel I forgot I had. That's going straight into the emergency fund. I'm starting to think of these canceled subscriptions as small leaks in a boat. Every time I find one and plug it, the boat floats a little higher. I'm running out of leaks to find, though. That's a good sign, I think.
entries.highlight: Set up rent autopay and canceled a forgotten cable package, redirecting the savings to the emergency fund.

entries.title: White chicken chili, too salty
entries.body: Tried a new recipe tonight: white chicken chili, with white beans, green chiles, cumin, and shredded chicken. I've made Mom's red chili so many times now that I wanted to try something different. It was a good idea, mostly. The problem is that I used regular broth and also salted it like I normally do, and the recipe was written for low-sodium broth. Way too much salt. I ate a bowl and drank about four glasses of water. I fixed it a little by adding another can of beans and some sour cream, but it's still pretty salty. I'll adjust next time. I'll definitely make it again, though, because underneath the salt it was really good, creamy and warm. It's 48 degrees out and it felt like the right food. I'm writing low sodium broth on the recipe in pen.
entries.highlight: Tried a new white chicken chili recipe that came out too salty but was promising enough to make again.

entries.title: Evening walk to the lighthouse
entries.body: After dinner, and after all that water, I needed to walk off the salt, so I took a long walk on the lake path to the little lighthouse at the end of the pier. It's about two miles round trip. It was already dark at 6:30, and the lighthouse blinks green every four seconds, which I counted on the way. The wind off the lake was really cold, colder than I expected, and I had to zip my jacket up over my chin. Walking fast with the wind at my back, I felt good, actually. My legs were still a little heavy from last week's weights, but the cold kept me moving. There were only a few other people out there, a couple holding hands and a guy feeding the ducks. I liked how quiet it was. I'll come back here.
entries.favorite: The green blink every four seconds
entries.highlight: Took a long evening walk along the lake path to the lighthouse at the end of the pier.

entries.title: The dark is coming back
entries.body: Skipped the Wednesday swim and went to bed at 9:30. It's not because I'm sick or because of a launch. It's just that it got dark at 6:20 and something in me shut off. I remember this feeling from last year: the hibernation thing. I sat on the couch at 7 and couldn't move, and then I was in bed at 9:30. My body was telling me to slow down, but I'm not sure it was telling the truth this time. Sometimes it's rest and sometimes it's just the dark. I'm going to try to keep at least one swim a week through the winter, no matter what. That's the deal I'm making with myself. One swim minimum. Also I'm buying one of those light lamps Priya told me about, which she says nurses on night shift swear by.
entries.highlight: Skipped a swim as early darkness brought back a familiar winter slump and set a minimum goal of one swim a week.

entries.title: Low-sodium broth, top of the list
entries.body: Went to the grocery store at 8:15, before the stroller crowd. Stuck to the list for once, and first on the list was low sodium broth, written in capital letters like the onions last year. Got salmon, oat milk, rice, yogurt, broth, a butternut squash, chicken thighs, spinach, and apples. $78. The big store has an aisle of fall stuff now, with pumpkins and gourds stacked up outside, and I almost bought a pumpkin for no reason. I didn't. Discipline. Then I came home and roasted the squash for soup while doing the crossword. It's 41 degrees and the sky is very gray, and the apartment still has more light than my old one did on a sunny day. I'm trying to remember that this winter, when it gets dark early. The light is still here. It's just shorter.
entries.highlight: Stuck to the grocery list, including low-sodium broth, and made squash soup on a gray morning.

entries.title: Ethiopian dinner with Priya
entries.body: Priya had a rare weeknight off, so we got dinner at the Ethiopian place around the corner from our building. It's the kind of place with eight tables and a hand-written menu, and the owner calls Priya by name. We got the vegetarian combination and ate with our hands, tearing the injera, which Priya showed me how to do without getting lentils on my sleeve. I got lentils on my sleeve. We talked about everything. Her night shifts, my phase two launch, her family in Toronto, my Dad's knee, and which neighbor in the building plays the trumpet at 6pm. It's the guy on the third floor, apparently. We stayed until they closed at 10 and laughed so hard about the trumpet guy that the owner brought us free tea. It's nice to have a friend who lives fifteen steps away.
entries.highlight: Had a long dinner with neighbor Priya at a local Ethiopian restaurant and became closer friends.

entries.title: Yoga instead of the couch
entries.body: Did yoga after work at the new gym. After last week's hibernation night, I made myself a rule: if I don't feel like swimming, I go to yoga instead, because yoga is basically lying down with extra steps. That's what got me there. The instructor at this gym is a soft-spoken man named Hal who plays rain sounds, and the room is lit with these warm lamps, which is probably exactly what my winter brain needs. We did a lot of twists. Apparently my spine has been stiff since the move. The balance poses went surprisingly well, and I didn't fall into anyone this time. Hal told us to breathe into the twist, so I did, mostly by sighing loudly. I walked home under the streetlights. The light lamp I ordered comes Monday. Small steps against the dark.
entries.highlight: Chose yoga over staying home to fight off the winter slump and felt stronger than expected.

entries.title: Halloween walk and a single bag of candy
entries.body: Long walk before work this morning, on the lake path, in the cold. There were pumpkins on almost every stoop on my street, and someone had dressed the lighthouse at the end of the pier in a giant fake spiderweb. My legs were stiff in the cold, but my head was clear, which I needed for the Friday design review. Tonight was my first Halloween in a building where kids actually trick-or-treat. In the old place, nobody climbed three flights for candy. Here, Priya and I sat on the front steps with one bag of candy each, and we both ran out by 6:45. I was totally unprepared. A tiny dragon was very disappointed in me. Lesson learned: next year, two bags, at least. Maybe three. The dragon will not be disappointed again.
entries.highlight: Took a morning walk and spent Halloween evening handing out candy with Priya, running out by 6:45.

entries.title: Garlic planted, one year later
entries.body: Called Mom on the walk home. It was dark already, 5:10. Mom spent the weekend putting the garden to bed and planting garlic, which she did last year too. She reminded me of what she said then, that garlic rewards patience. She said, look at you, you were patient. You moved. I think she's right. A year ago on this same call I was complaining about my dark apartment and my takeout spending, and now I'm calling her from a street with orange maples, on my way home to an apartment with good light. She sent me home in October with a jar of her chives, and they're still alive on my windowsill, which she considers a miracle. Dad says hi. His knee is bad, and he goes to the doctor next week, and Mom thinks the doctor's going to push PT again.
entries.highlight: Had a reflective call with Mom while she planted garlic, comparing how much has changed since last year.

entries.title: Flu shot at the slow pharmacy
entries.body: Ran errands after work. The pharmacy first, for my flu shot. The pharmacy here is, as promised, good but slow. I waited thirty minutes in a row of plastic chairs, then got the shot from a pharmacist who told me about her son's soccer team the whole time, which was a nice distraction. My arm is sore. I also refilled my prescription while I was there, since I finally learned to do them both at once. Then the post office, where the line was long, but the cat was asleep on a pile of padded envelopes, so I didn't mind. Mailed Mom a birthday card for next week. Then the corner store for a box of tea. Three stops in under an hour, even with the slow pharmacy. I'm getting good at the new route.
entries.highlight: Got a flu shot, refilled a prescription, and mailed Mom a birthday card on an efficient evening errand run.

entries.title: Retro on the phase two launch
entries.body: The 8:05 was fifteen minutes late, because of a signal problem. Cleared my inbox on the platform, holding my phone with gloves on, which doesn't work, so I took one off and lost feeling in my fingers. Got in just in time for the retro on the phase two launch. It went well. The numbers are good, a bit smaller than phase one but still real. I let Chloe run the retro, which is the first time she's run any meeting, and she was nervous for about two minutes and then completely fine. She asked the team what we would never do again, and everyone laughed, and then gave honest answers. Afterward, Dana stopped by my desk and said, you're growing people now, not just designs. I wrote that down. Ate lunch at my desk again, but only because it was raining.
entries.highlight: Let mentee Chloe run the phase two launch retro, and Dana praised Jordan for developing people.

entries.title: Alex is looking at rings
entries.body: Got coffee with Alex this morning near the office. We did our two laps of the block in the cold, both holding our coffees like hand warmers. And then Alex said, I've been looking at rings. Very quietly, like Robin might be hiding behind a mailbox. Alex said it's going to be in the spring, probably March, when they go back to the place they had their first date, a little restaurant up north with a view of a waterfall. Alex showed me photos of three rings on their phone and asked which one I liked, and I said the second, and Alex said that's the one I like too. We talked about the July coffee when Alex first said Robin is it. I said I'm not surprised at all, again. Alex made me swear to secrecy. I'm writing it here, which doesn't count.
entries.favorite: Alex whispering like Robin was behind a mailbox
entries.highlight: Had coffee with Alex, who confided they are ring shopping and planning to propose to Robin in the spring.

entries.title: No space heater this winter
entries.body: Paid rent and the bills, or rather checked that autopay worked, which it did. The building turned the heat on this week and my apartment is actually warm. In the old place I used a space heater from November to March, and I just remembered that and looked it up: that space heater added about $30 a month to my electric bill in the winter. So I sold it online tonight for $25 to a student, who seemed very excited. I also found a language app I'd paid for annually and completely forgotten. I got a refund for the unused months because I asked, which is apparently something you can do. $41 back. I'm learning that asking is a skill, whether it's for a refund, a project, or the promotion Alex got. It's the same muscle.
entries.favorite: Getting a refund just by asking
entries.highlight: Sold an old space heater, canceled a forgotten app subscription, and got a refund just by asking.

entries.title: Dad agreed to physical therapy
entries.body: Dad called me tonight, which is the second time ever, I think. Last December was the first, when he called to complain that his doctor wanted him to do physical therapy. Tonight he called to say he went to the doctor today and, quote, the knee is not just old, it's a problem. The doctor gave him two options: physical therapy, starting in January, twice a week for three months, or start talking about surgery. He picked physical therapy. He said it like he was announcing his retirement. I told him I was proud of him, and he grumbled, but I could tell he liked hearing it. Mom got on the phone afterward and whispered, thank you for not saying I told you so. I didn't say it, but I did think it. Dad says the garden can wait till spring.
entries.favorite: Dad calling to tell me himself
entries.highlight: Dad called to share that he finally agreed to start physical therapy for his knee in January.

entries.title: Sprint planning that could have been an email
entries.body: Started with sprint planning, which ran an hour and forty minutes over. We spent forty minutes of that debating whether one ticket was a three or a five. It was a three. I knew it was a three. Frankly, the whole thing could have been an email. Got nothing else done until 3. But I did something different this time: at the end, I suggested we try a shorter format next sprint, with tickets estimated before the meeting. A year ago I would have just complained about it here and never said anything out loud. Dana said, great, you can draft the new format. So that's what happens when you speak up. You get homework. Still worth it. Left at 5:30 anyway, walked home from the station in the cold, and made soup.
entries.highlight: Sat through an overlong sprint planning meeting and spoke up to propose a shorter format.

entries.title: Coat drive at the community center
entries.body: After the long sprint planning day, I did one quick errand: the community center down the street is running a winter coat drive, and I had two coats sitting in the hall closet that I haven't worn since the move. One is the puffy green one I wore every day in the old apartment because it was warmer than the apartment itself. The other is a wool coat that was too small even when I bought it. I brought them in, along with a bag of hats and gloves, and the woman at the table thanked me like I'd done something heroic. It took ten minutes. The hall closet looks huge now, or at least it closes all the way, which is a big improvement. It's a funny feeling to give away the coat that got me through the dark apartment. I hope it keeps someone else warm.
entries.favorite: The hall closet closing all the way
entries.highlight: Donated two old winter coats and accessories to a community center coat drive.

entries.title: Sam's first interview didn't go anywhere
entries.body: Met Sam for dinner at the dumpling place, my old one, because Sam wanted comfort food and so did I. The counter guy said, long time, and gave us extra chili oil. Sam had their first real interview last week, at an education nonprofit, and found out today that they didn't get it. Sam was disappointed but weirdly okay. They said the interview made them realize they actually want this, which they weren't sure about before, so it was worth it. I told Sam about my first apartment viewing, the cozy closet one, and how the first one is just practice for the right one. Sam said, that's very wise for someone with chili oil on their chin. We stayed until close and got so loud about the pivot couch that we nearly knocked over the soy sauce. Made plans to do it again soon.
entries.favorite: Extra chili oil from the counter guy
entries.highlight: Had a comforting dinner with Sam after Sam's first job interview didn't work out.

entries.title: Mom's birthday cake, made by Dad
entries.body: Called Mom this morning, the day after her birthday, because yesterday she was too busy to talk. Apparently, Dad made her a cake. Dad does not bake. He has never baked. He found a recipe for a lemon cake in one of her cookbooks and made it entirely by himself, sitting on a stool at the counter because of his knee. Mom said it was lopsided, sank in the middle, and was the best cake she's ever eaten. She got my card, the one I mailed from the post office with the cat, and she put it on the fridge. We talked about Thanksgiving. I'm on stuffing and pie again, obviously, and this year I'm making the crust from scratch for real. She said, we'll see, in exactly the same voice as last year. I cleaned the whole kitchen while we talked.
entries.highlight: Called Mom after her birthday and heard that Dad baked her a cake for the first time.

entries.title: The dark-month takeout creep
entries.body: Monthly budget check-in this afternoon, and I'll be honest, the eating out line is creeping up again. $218 so far in November, with two weeks left. It's not as bad as last year, but I can see what's happening. It gets dark at 4:45, I get home tired, and the phone is right there, and the Thai place delivers in twenty minutes. Last year it was $412, so I'm not going to spiral. But I also don't want to slide backward. So here's the plan. I'm going to make sure there's always one frozen meal in the freezer, something I made myself, for the nights when cooking feels impossible. A soup or chili I can just heat up. That way the option that's easiest isn't the most expensive one. Groceries are fine. Moved $150 to savings anyway.
entries.highlight: Noticed winter takeout spending creeping back up and planned to keep homemade frozen meals on hand.

entries.title: Hal's yoga, the only workout this week
entries.body: Did yoga after work with Hal, the rain sounds instructor. It's the only workout I've done this week, and it's Wednesday. I've missed both swims. The deal I made with myself in October was one swim minimum a week, and I'm barely holding on to it. Something about the cold water when it's dark outside feels impossible right now. Yoga is easier because the room is warm and the lights are low, and the hardest pose is basically a nap. My legs are going to hurt tomorrow anyway, from a long series of lunges that Hal called gentle, which was a lie, the same lie as last January's gentle flow class. Yoga teachers all use the same dictionary. I walked home feeling looser. The light lamp has been helping in the mornings, a bit. I'm going to try for a Saturday swim.
entries.highlight: Went to yoga as the only workout of the week while struggling to keep up swimming in the dark season.

entries.title: A holiday budget, before the holidays
entries.body: Did something I've never done before: I made a holiday gift budget before buying a single gift. Last year I just kind of bought things as I went, and then I was shocked in January. This year the limit is $300 total. Mom, Dad, Sam, Alex, Priya, Chloe, and something small for Ravi and Marcus. I made a little list in the spreadsheet with a column for ideas, a column for prices, and a column for done. For Dad, I'm thinking a really good ice and heat wrap for his knee, since PT starts in January. For Mom, a book about building raised garden beds, because she's been talking about one. For Priya, a nice herb drying rack. I also moved some money into savings. The emergency fund is at $1,860. That's about two months less scary than it was in October. It's slowly becoming a real cushion.
entries.highlight: Set a $300 holiday gift budget in advance and planned thoughtful gifts for family and friends.

entries.title: Opening the misc boxes, finally
entries.body: Spent the morning finally dealing with the last four boxes, the ones labeled misc, which have been sitting in the bedroom closet since September like a threat. It took two hours. Box one: cords, again, even after I threw out nine in March. Box two: photos and letters, including a card from Mom from my college graduation, which made me sit on the floor for a while. Box three: random kitchen things, like a garlic press I didn't know I owned. Box four: the lobster hat. So that's where it went. Then I organized the closet, folded everything, and put the empty boxes in the recycling room downstairs. It's the first time since the move that every single thing I own has a place. Also took out the recycling. Three months to unpack four boxes. To be fair, about right.
entries.highlight: Finally unpacked the last four boxes from the move, three months later, and organized the closet.

entries.title: Short-week meal prep with frozen pesto
entries.body: Meal-prepped lunches for the short week before Thanksgiving. I only need three, since I'm leaving Wednesday afternoon, so I made pasta with pesto. But not jar pesto. Back in October I froze Priya's basil pesto in an ice cube tray, which is a trick she taught me, and tonight I just popped out six cubes and melted them into the pasta with some roasted broccoli and white beans. Took about forty-five minutes instead of two hours. Tuesday me, who has three meetings in a row, is going to be very grateful. Also, this is the start of the frozen meal plan: I made a double batch of the white chicken chili, with low sodium broth this time, and put four portions in the freezer. Emergency rations for the dark nights. Not too salty. I checked. Twice.
entries.highlight: Meal-prepped a short week of lunches with frozen homemade pesto and stocked the freezer with chili.

entries.title: Thanksgiving: the crust held
entries.body: Thanksgiving at my parents'. I came up yesterday on the 3:10 train with my rolling pin in my bag, which got me a strange look from the conductor. This year I made the pie crust from scratch, for real. I practiced twice at home, once a disaster and once fine, and today it rolled out in one piece, and it held, and Mom watched me crimp the edges and didn't say hmm once. The pie was apple, with a lattice top. The stuffing had the sourdough from the farmers market and fresh sage from Priya's balcony. Dad sat at the head of the table with his cane leaning on the chair next to him, and when he took the first bite of pie, he said it was the best one yet, which he says every year, but this year I believe him. Mom asked for the crust recipe. I'm framing that moment.
entries.highlight: Made the Thanksgiving stuffing and a from-scratch pie crust that held together, impressing Mom at their parents' house.

entries.title: Black Friday: bought one thing
entries.body: Took the train home this morning with a container of leftover turkey and three slices of pie. Checked the bills when I got home. Autopay did its thing, rent, electric, internet. I also set up autopay for the gas bill, the last utility I'd missed, because this building bills it separately and I had no idea until the first one came. Yesterday was Black Friday, and in other years I'd have bought five things I didn't need. This year I bought exactly one: the knee wrap for Dad, on my list, at thirty percent off. That's it. Then I closed the laptop. My holiday budget spreadsheet now has one checkmark in the done column, and $62 subtracted from the $300. Mom gave me a bag of frozen tomato sauce on my way out, which is technically another holiday gift, and free.
entries.favorite: One checkmark in the done column
entries.highlight: Set up autopay for the gas bill and bought only one planned gift on Black Friday, staying on budget.

entries.title: Sunday stir-fry, no recipe needed
entries.body: Made a stir-fry for dinner tonight, and I realized halfway through that I didn't look at a recipe at all. I just knew it. Tofu pressed under the cookbook, crisped in the cast iron in two batches, then onions, bell pepper, snap peas, a handful of spinach. The sauce is my standard now, soy sauce, garlic, ginger, honey, rice vinegar, and a spoon of chili crisp. Back in April, this was a big experiment I was proud of. Now it's just a Sunday. I think that's what learning to cook actually is. The first time, it's an event, and then one day it's just dinner. Monday and Tuesday lunch, handled. I sat at my little table by the window while it got dark at 4:30 and the street lights came on one by one, and the snow started, just a little.
entries.highlight: Made a stir-fry from memory without a recipe and reflected on how cooking has become routine.

entries.title: Leftover turkey congee
entries.body: Tried a new recipe tonight with the leftover turkey from Mom's: turkey congee. Ravi told me about it at lunch, his grandmother's go-to after Thanksgiving. You simmer rice in a lot of broth for about an hour and a half until it breaks down into a thick porridge, then add shredded turkey, ginger, scallions, soy sauce, and a soft-boiled egg on top. I was skeptical, since rice porridge sounded like something you eat in the hospital. It is not. It's the coziest thing I've ever made. It's 28 degrees out and snowing again, and I ate a big bowl of it on the couch with a blanket over my knees. This is going into the permanent file. I took a photo and sent it to Ravi, who replied with my grandmother approves. I don't know how he knows that. But I'll take it.
entries.highlight: Made turkey congee from Thanksgiving leftovers using coworker Ravi's family recipe.

entries.title: November's number: $246
entries.body: Monthly budget check-in for November. Eating out was $246. That's the highest since August, which was the moving month, so I can't blame moving. It was the dark. But here's the thing: it's still about $170 less than last November. And the frozen chili plan started working in the last week, since I had two nights where I was about to order and ate the chili instead. So I'm going to call it a partial win. Groceries came in at $250, normal. I moved some money into savings, $200, and the emergency fund is at $2,060. I'm noticing I'm calmer about the bad months. Last year a bad month made me want to throw the spreadsheet out the window. Now it's just a number that tells me what happened, and what to try next. That feels like a big shift.
entries.highlight: Reviewed November's higher takeout spending calmly and noted it was still far below last year's.

entries.title: Salmon on a Friday, no fear
